title: fleet: a stub-agent seam for a seat that COMMITS and then dies, and the live crash re-dispatch arm on it (tinytown-tnkuq.73's AC2)
notes:
Filed by builder-2 at the review of tinytown-tnkuq.73, 2026-09-13, on Alberto's ruling in session: land tinytown-tnkuq.73's AC1 and AC3 and carry AC2 here.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD. tinytown-tnkuq.73's AC2 asks for the crash re-dispatch proved live on the scratch project through the shipped binary: a stub builder that commits one file and then exits mid-turn, whose re-dispatched successor's worktree HEAD equals that commit. It could not be built inside that slice because THE SEAM DOES NOT EXIST, measured at 6f9143908: fleet/cli/tests/flight.rs carries exactly two stub behaviours, logged-out (with logged-out-live) and kill-when-assigned, and the word crash does not occur in that file at all — control: it occurs in fleet/cli/tests/drive.rs and fleet/cli/tests/workspace.rs, so the read is absence and not a broken needle. kill-when-assigned dies BEFORE any commit, which is the one thing AC2's case cannot be: the re-dispatch cuts from the branch's last commit, so the seat must have committed first.

WHAT LANDS HERE. A stub-agent behaviour that commits a file and then exits in a way the controller writes session.crashed for, and the live arm on it. The seam is the reusable half — every later crash arm wants it, and tinytown-tnkuq.20's rehearsal exercises the same path.

COST, measured on this box 2026-09-13, so nobody plans this as a small one: fleet-cli flight arms run 8 to 30 minutes each; the full suite is 832 arms in 1653s with 67 already marked slow.

A FLAKE TO FIX OR AVOID IN THE SAME NEIGHBOURHOOD, found while building tinytown-tnkuq.73: fleet-cli::flight::a_loop_killed_between_a_dispatch_and_its_event_restarts_without_dispatching_twice hung 102 minutes against a 494s baseline. Its fixture carries 7 events and no session.crashed at all, and its stub builder lost a git add race so fleet deliver answered 'nothing is staged' 120 times. Not this bead's subject, but it is the arm nearest to the one being written.

THE HONEST PART: tinytown-tnkuq.73's readiness pass, written by this seat, answered READY 3 yes. READY 3 asks that every criterion name the command and the exit code that proves it. AC2 names a live arm whose fixture does not exist, so it was not provable as written and the pass should have caught it. Recorded here because the next readiness pass on a live arm should ask whether the seam it needs is on the tree.
HELD (architect-2, 2026-09-17, tinytown-tnkuq.92): deferred, not closed. This defect lives in the flight's advance or fly machinery, which the fleet-layers direction turns into the core run lifecycle (pin, lock, cap, resume, retire-all) with composition moving to tiny's workflows. Whether this code survives, moves or is replaced is the workflows sitting's to say; the bug is real and measured and comes back to open if the code it names survives the MVP. Deferred so the ready pool stops offering work on code whose fate is undecided.
Moved from the tinytown board on 2026-09-22, where it was tinytown-ppjwc; that bead is closed there with a pointer here. Edges to beads that stayed on the tinytown board, not carried across: discovered-from tinytown-tnkuq.73.
close_reason: Obsolete: deferred until it was known whether the code it names survives the MVP. It did not: the flight advance and fleet fly/plan/autopilot left core at tinytown fd7f6a47a (2026-09-17; see core/src/lib.rs:83). The crash re-dispatch arm it seams for belonged to the advance. If the run lifecycle grows crash re-dispatch, carry the need for a commit-then-die stub seam into that design (see closed fleet-biilb).

title: [epic] fleet, built in-house: the controller and the plugin shape in fleet/ until the phase-A gate — the lessons documents, the scaffold, the PRD's five slices — every fleet bead until the leave (Alberto's D8 on tinytown-ui3u9, 2026-09-05; brain/fleet-migration.md §5 A2–A4)
description:
## Why

Alberto's ruling 2026-09-05 (D8 on tinytown-ui3u9, verbatim option label "All of fleet in-house; gc after it leaves"): fleet — the controller, the cli and the packs — is built by tinytown's own seats in fleet/ at this repo's root, on this board, until it can build itself and leaves for Tinytown/fleet as one snapshot (D10). brain/fleet-migration.md §5 A2–A4 is the sequence; the fleet-controller PRD at fleet/docs/prds/fleet-controller-prd.md is what the slices build. This epic holds every fleet bead until the leave; the fleet label is the queue (bd list --label fleet).

## What

Children, in landing order — each one bead wide until its prerequisite has landed (brain/architect-role.md, the fan-out rule): the lessons documents (A2 step 2), the scaffold (A2 step 3), then the PRD's slices 1–5 and the plugin shape (A4), each a spec bead by an architect. The phase-A gate closes the epic: fleet's controller starts a builder, observes it to delivery and retires it, on a fleet bead, with the porter untouched (plan §5 A4, the gate).

## Rules for every child

- Nothing under fleet/ references tinytown: no bead id, no path, no seat name; grep -rci tinytown fleet/ reads 0 at every landing (Alberto, 2026-09-05, on tinytown-tvw64). Commit subjects carry the bead id by house rule and never leave (plan §5 B0).
- Written new, the porter read and never copied (D6); the lessons documents are read before the PRD's requirement is built.
- Stdlib-class dependencies only (PRD Q1): a TOML reader and a JSON writer are the only crates permitted.
- Gate line on every child: touched suites green; reviewer runs the full suite at landing.

## Success Criteria

- SC1 The phase-A gate as brain/fleet-migration.md §5 A4 states it: fleet's controller, a second user service beside the porter, dispatches a fleet bead to a builder it started, observes it to delivery and retires it, once in auto mode and once under dontAsk, with the porter untouched — recorded on the closing child with the projection and event-stream excerpts that prove each verb.
- SC2 Every child landed through tools/land with its fleetmake rows green; grep -rci tinytown fleet/ reads 0 on main at the close.
- SC3 The leave (plan §5 B0) is filed as its own bead, discovered-from this epic, before this epic closes.
notes:
CHILDREN FILED (architect-1, 2026-09-05, under tinytown-gmkie, Alberto's order for the phase-A board): tinytown-tnkuq.4–.9 (controller slices 2–5, install and create, the self-build gate), .10–.16 (core: format and registry, guards, dispatch and brief, deliver and review, land, core's first gate, fly and autopilot), .17 (the plugin shape), .19 (tinytown's project.toml), .20 (the rehearsal), .23 (the switch), .24 (the tiny-fleet pack). Every one a FRAME owing its SPEC PASS and readiness pass before dispatch. Blocks edges child-to-child along the two spines only.

SC1 RE-READ under D12 (Alberto, 2026-09-05, tinytown-gmkie): the epic closes at the REHEARSAL (tinytown-tnkuq.20 — fleet flies one national flight of tinytown beads with the porter stopped), not at the self-build gate; the self-build gate (tinytown-tnkuq.9) and core's first gate (tinytown-tnkuq.15) are gates inside the phase. SC3 is met by tinytown-tnkuq.23 (the switch), filed as a child rather than a discovered-from sibling. brain/departure-board.md lays the children out as flights 1–10.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08, in architect-2's session, mechanism: fleet-workspace-shape, verbatim): "the workspace with three crates and one binary it is" — the cli is not a separate project: a Cargo workspace at fleet/ with fleet-core, fleet-controller and a thin fleet cli crate producing the one fleet binary; the options and the application are on tinytown-tnkuq.10, whose Why reserved the decision, and the workspace scaffold is filed as a child of this epic and .10's prerequisite (this note's next line names it).
The workspace scaffold is tinytown-tnkuq.25; tinytown-tnkuq.10 now depends on it.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T17:36Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-start-stop-and-status, verbatim): "fleet start | stop: should start and stop the controller" and "fleet runway: can be folder into status"
The seat's reading, for the cli PRD this session is drafting: fleet start loads the installed user service and fleet stop unloads it — the "load is a second deliberate act" the controller PRD's install requirement reserves, given its verb pair; fleet install writes and never starts, as before. fleet runway is not a command: its reading (each seat's context against the rest threshold, the window left) is a section of fleet status, which already prints the projection and the switch. Both apply to the frames tinytown-tnkuq.8 (install and create) and tinytown-tnkuq.16 (status) at their spec passes.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T17:49Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-nouns-seat-and-event, verbatim): "fleet clear-halt: sounds good" (to folding it under fleet event); "feed spawn: can it live under fleet seat spawn?"; "fleet retire: same as above fleet seat retire?"; "fleet install: could this be done as part of the command that installs fleet itself? this gets into how fleet is installed which is a different conversation. this could also run the first time that fleet start is invoked. pi uses `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh` for install"; "fleet fly and prime: look good"; "fleet courier: i like that you used ring in that sentence. i guess either ping or ring could work, your choice."
The seat's reading, for the cli PRD: two nouns. fleet seat is what is DONE to a seat — fleet seat spawn --first-turn, fleet seat feed <seat> --first-turn, fleet seat retire <seat> [--dead] (controller PRD R30–R32 unchanged in substance; tinytown-tnkuq.7's frame renames), and fleet seat ring <seat> --text (the packs PRD's P1 courier; ring chosen over ping because a ring is a doorbell and carries no authority, the fleet's own word for it). fleet event is what a seat SAYS — woke|rest|handed-off|exited, and now clear-halt <seat> as the person's request the controller consumes on its tick (controller PRD R14's remedy; spelled clear-halt and not revive, because revive is already the controller's own verdict for adopt-in-place and one word for two things is the drift this harness exists to catch). fleet install leaves the command surface: its work — the user service written, the machine directory created, telemetry asked — runs either inside the installer script or on the first fleet start, decided in the install conversation Alberto named; tinytown-tnkuq.8's frame carries this note at its spec pass. fleet fly, fleet autopilot and fleet prime stand as listed.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T17:52Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-item-and-verb-shape, AskUserQuestion answers verbatim): "item (Recommended)" for the word the verbs act on — "we need to settle on a name for beads that is not beads … beads is both too specific (we could support other memory layers in the future) and abstract (there are formulas and memory beads under it)"; and "Top-level: fleet dispatch <item> (Recommended)" for the verb shape.
The seat's reading, for the cli PRD: the work unit is an ITEM everywhere a person reads — help text, notes, the flight record — and the id the verbs take is an item id; bd stays the store beneath it and is named only where the store itself is meant. The four verbs and brief are top-level words: fleet dispatch <item>, fleet brief <item>, fleet deliver, fleet review <item>, fleet land <item>; fleet fly and fleet autopilot on|off beside them. Declined: task (collides with bd's issue type), work (no count noun), cargo (the analogy, and the Rust tool's name), and nesting the four under an item noun (symmetry bought with length on the most-typed verbs). Alberto's standing instruction for the PRD, verbatim: "i just want to make sure every command is explained in detail".
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T17:57Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-surface-closed, verbatim): "great lets add those two as well. fleet observe: lgtm / fleet event: lgtm / fleet doctor: lgtm / fleet pack search: lgtm / fleet --version: lgtm"
The seat's reading, closing the cli PRD's command inventory: fleet pack gains remove <source> (deletes the pack directory and drops its packs.lock table keyed by the source as typed; refuses core and any pack another installed pack imports) and list (packs.lock as a table — source, version, commit, fetched). fleet observe [--once] stays as the foreground form of the controller loop beside start and stop. fleet event carries the writers (woke|rest|handed-off|exited, clear-halt) and the readers (tail [--follow] [--since <seq>] [--seat] [--type], show <id>); the readers are a frame of their own. fleet doctor (P1) and fleet pack search (P2) stand as the PRDs place them. fleet --version stays. Surface at this note: nine families — lifecycle (create, start, stop, status), seat (spawn, feed, retire, ring), event (six writers and readers), item verbs (dispatch, brief, deliver, review, land), flight (fly, autopilot), hooks (guard, prime), orders (list, check, run, history), packs (add, check, remove, list, search), and observe with --version. Standing instruction for the PRD text: every command explained in detail.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T18:06Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-nudge-not-ring, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim: "nudge (Recommended)"): the courier verb is fleet seat nudge <seat> --text. The naming doc's row for waking a live seat with a message already reads nudge and lists courier among the coinages not carried over, so ring — chosen earlier in this sitting and recorded under cli-nouns-seat-and-event — is withdrawn: one word for one mechanism, the controller's threshold nudge and the person's message on the same adapter path. tinytown-tnkuq.34 is retitled.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T18:30Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-ui-crates, verbatim): "document somewhere or file a bead for flight 5. indicatif for progress on fly and land, console for styled status lines, dialoguer for create's two questions"
The seat's reading: filed as tinytown-tnkuq.36 on flight 5, the three crates entering fleet-cli through one ui module with a stated policy (plain on a pipe, NO_COLOR or a dumb terminal; progress on stderr past two seconds; prompts refuse a pipe naming the flag), first uses on the verbs built today, and the fly, land and create frames carrying a note each naming the surface they take. comfy-table not taken; ratatui is the manager's question and not the cli's.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T18:58Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: manager-api-shape, verbatim): "If fleet publishes one, it should be generated from the same Rust types the cli uses, with a crate such as utoipa deriving the schema from the handlers, so the cli and the API cannot disagree, and it should be a handful of paths, loopback by default, over the two files that are already the record"
The seat's reading: settled ahead of the manager's design session, filed as fleet-tnkuq.37 under this epic — one definition of the surface in Rust types shared by the cli and the API, the schema generated and never hand-written, a small path count, loopback unless turned on, every read from the projection and the event stream; the SSE transport of the controller PRD's P1 is the stream's network form. The sitting decides where the manager runs, its paths, its writes, its exposure, its screen and the premium line (Q1–Q6 on the bead).
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T19:45Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: log-and-stats-one-prd, verbatim): "ok so log and stats deserver their own prds or maybe one prd for both since they're part of the same story"
The seat's reading: one PRD for the two, filed as fleet-tnkuq.38 under this epic — the record as a product and the numbers folded over it, because stats has no input but the log; the settled list and the seven questions are on the bead. Off the departure board: the log and stats are pieces after phase A, like the manager.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: vision-primitives-not-features, AskUserQuestion clarification verbatim): "Primitives, not features" — the vision page's "Primitives, not a platform" bullet is retitled to that heading, the phrase pi.dev leads its own extensibility section with, chosen after reading that page as the reference for how fleet should feel: a foundation that unlocks customization on top. Declined: "A foundation, not a framework" (the seat's recommendation), keeping the old heading with a rewritten body, and "Simple, local, and truly yours" as the heading (that line leads fleet/docs/integrations.md instead). The body under the new heading and the integrations page that is its long form land together on the bead filed for the page.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-is-the-name, verbatim): "cockpit it is, great." — the piece the vision page calls fleet-manager is named cockpit: the product's fourth flying word, allowed under the naming doc's rule because the content is an instrument panel (a bar of gauges and alerts, a status readout, a seat held while autopilot flies) and it is used everywhere without variation. The rename touches the vision page, the naming doc's row for the screen, and the design bead's title, and lands with the cockpit PRD. Declined: manager (plain, says nothing, collides with the job title and with process managers).
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-server-in-the-binary, verbatim): "where the server goes is a great question. i'll take your recommendation here. my only request is that it should behave similar to docker. the app can be closed while the server is still running and you would see the fleet icon up on the notification bar with a menu that has items like quit server, stop controller, open cockpit. the server should be able to run even if the app is not open." — the recommendation taken: the typed API's handlers live in one library crate; the one binary gains a serve verb that runs them over HTTP on loopback, so a headless box serves a phone with no window; the cockpit is a web app in a Tauri shell that calls the same handlers as Tauri commands on the desktop and embeds the server. The Docker Desktop shape is the requirement: closing the window leaves the server running, a fleet icon sits in the menu bar (macOS) or the system tray (Linux) with at least quit server, stop controller and open cockpit, and the server runs with no app open. Declined: an HTTP surface in the controller (the controller PRD's non-goal stands); a separate product that only reads the two files.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-economy-warning, verbatim): "economy: i meant the economy.level in fleet.toml" — the economy warning in the cockpit's settings screen is against dialing economy.level (SM | MD | LG, the reference's spend dial, brain/harness/fleet.md) up when the account runway will not reach the horizon; the cap on concurrent flights is the same reading's other arm. The seat's reading: economy.level enters the fleet's fleet.toml as a policy key the cockpit reads and writes, the runway reading is an adapter measurement of account usage folded with the stream's cost events (the log-and-stats sitting's cost question), the warning is the cockpit's before a save, and the refusal is fly's and the autopilot pull's — the cockpit shows the record and holds no belief of its own.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-serve-and-launch, verbatim): "the app's first launch just like docker when you launch the mac app. you should also be able to launch via fleet serve with the icon appearing in the bar but the app itself not launching" — launching the cockpit app starts the server the way Docker Desktop's first launch starts its daemon, and fleet serve from a shell starts the server with the menu-bar icon shown and no window opened. The seat's reading: the server and the tray icon are one resident process with two modes, tray-only and windowed; fleet serve starts it tray-only, launching the app starts it windowed or shows the window of the one already running, and both are idempotent; the window is a view over the resident process and closing it returns to tray-only. The resident process is the login-item shape, so a closet machine serves a phone across a reboot. Build question left for the PRD, with the seat's recommendation: the cockpit app is the resident process and fleet serve starts it in tray mode, so the fleet binary links no GUI toolkit and a display-less box takes a no-tray flag; declined by recommendation only, not by ruling: the tray drawn by the fleet binary itself.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-read-paths, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim): "#2 but i want to explain why, one view of the cockpit will be a task management feature similar to Linear but built for beads and agent orchestration" — Q2 of the manager bead: the four paths over the two files (status, events, stats, config) PLUS an item family reading the work graph, because one cockpit view is task management over the work graph itself. The seat's reading: the four verbs gain item events regardless (dispatched, delivered, reviewed, landed, returned, decision owed), since the stream is what the phone tails and what stats fold; the item family is more than one GET — a task view needs list and query (ready, blocked, by label, by assignee, the dependency edges) — and its types cannot be shared with bd's, which is Go, so they are fleet's Rust types over bd's --json output, the one place the "same types as the cli" rule reaches a store fleet does not own. Declined: the four alone with no item path; two paths.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-writes, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim): "The full verb surface" — Q3 of the manager bead: the API writes settings (policy keys to fleet.toml, machine keys such as accounts to the machine directory, never committed), autopilot on|off, an answer to a decision, and the verbs — dispatch, fly, nudge, retire — each through the handler the cli already has, so the API adds no writer of its own and every write reads itself back and exits by the one table. With the task view (cockpit-read-paths) the item family writes too: create, update, claim, close, dep add, through bd. Declined: read-only; the three writes alone.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-exposure, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim): "Loopback, LAN by key with a paired token (Recommended)" — Q4 of the manager bead: loopback by default; one machine-local key binds the LAN; a token generated at first serve is paired from the settings screen by QR and carried by the phone; a remote bridge, if one exists, is a relay of the same server. Declined: off-machine only through a bridge; LAN open with no auth.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-premium-line, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim): "tbd, we shouldnt gate mobile access behind a paid tier" — Q6 of the manager bead stays open, with one constraint ruled: mobile access is never behind a paid tier. The vision page's sentence "The premium tier adds a bridge to your phone" and the fleet-manager section's "the door to the premium tier" no longer hold as written and are edited when the cockpit PRD lands. Declined: any second device as premium; the app itself as premium.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-view-line, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim: "Two tiers, no iframe (Recommended)", taken after a survey of twelve tools on fleet-tnkuq.37 and a closer read of pi.dev's slot-and-kit model): custom views in the cockpit have two tiers and no iframe. Tier one — views as declarative documents over a cockpit block vocabulary (list, table, board, gauge, timeline, detail, form, markdown, action at filing; the vocabulary grows with demand) bound to the API's typed paths and stream queries, rendered by the cockpit inside named slots the app owns, validated by a check verb, shipped in a pack, picked up from a file with no build step. Tier two — custom components as web components composed from the cockpit's own component library and semantic theme tokens, rendered in the page and never in a frame, with a check that refuses a component carrying a raw color, font or size. Taken from pi.dev whole: the slot model, the theme as semantic names an author uses and never sets, no build step and reload from a file, and "ask your seat to build it". Not taken: pi's free enforcement, which the terminal medium supplies and the web does not — hence the check. Declined: pi's model as is (code only); declarative only; three tiers with a sandboxed iframe (every rung-five host has the failure Alberto named: nothing but words keeps it on theme).
DATE CORRECTION (architect-2, 2026-09-08T22:33Z read from date -u): every note this seat wrote on this record today carrying the date 2026-09-09 — the rulings vision-primitives-not-features, cockpit-is-the-name, cockpit-server-in-the-binary, cockpit-serve-and-launch, cockpit-economy-warning, cockpit-read-paths, cockpit-writes, cockpit-exposure, cockpit-premium-line and cockpit-view-line on the epic, the sitting-opened, survey-opened and survey-findings notes on fleet-tnkuq.37, and the description and verdict on tinytown-tnkuq.39 — was written on 2026-09-08 between roughly 20:30Z and 22:30Z. The date was taken from the harness's own "today" line instead of the clock; the clock reads 2026-09-08. The content of every note stands; only the date in each is wrong by one day.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T22:43Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-attach-in-a-pane, verbatim): "it should open a pane inside the cockpit. we will define what a pane is down the road and how extensions can also leverage them" — the roster's attach opens the seat's conversation in a pane inside the cockpit, never in the user's tmux server or a separate terminal window. A pane is a cockpit primitive to be defined later, one that extensions can also use — so it joins the slot list the view-line ruling (cockpit-view-line) says the app owns, and the attach pane is its first occupant. The seat's reading: this makes attach a terminal surface inside a web view (a terminal emulator in the pane driven by the adapter's attach), which is the largest shape named on the design bead; tmux disappears as a requirement and the terminal policy key with it. Declined: the user's tmux server; a new terminal window.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T22:44Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-views-core-vs-tiny-fleet, verbatim): "once we get closer to building the cockpit we will hash out the details. there's one more thing related to this i want documented somewhere and that's the views that belong in the core pack vs what belongs in the tiny-fleet pack. also what should we name the folder that houses theses extensions inside a pack? what do others call it? each of these will be their own epic down the road since they're a huge amount of work / part of core: - Tasks (beads): linear for beads, inbox, filters, views, create beads using an agent window - Schedule (orders): see upcoming + past, edit, add - in V2 -> Review: git history, review commit later, diff, PRs, approve, decline, etc. (the idea here is to completely replace vscode and beadazzle as tools i have to jump between) / part of tiny-fleet: - Flights (runs): the departure board, currently flying and upcoming ones, this is the one feature that's opinionated about how the user should work. this is probably where creating and editing formulas will also live since it dictates what the flights do". The split as ruled: core's views are Tasks (the work graph as a Linear-shaped task manager: inbox, filters, saved views, creating items through an agent window), Schedule (orders: upcoming and past, edit, add) and, at V2, Review (git history, a commit's diff, PRs, approve and decline — the cockpit replacing the editor and the bd screen as places to jump between); tiny-fleet's view is Flights (runs: the departure board, what is flying and what is next, and where formulas are created and edited, since formulas dictate what a flight does) — the one view with an opinion about how a person should work, which is why it is a pack's. Each family is its own epic later. The home for this is the cockpit PRD (fleet-tnkuq.37 AC1), with the integrations page's pack section owing one sentence when it lands.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T22:47Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: pack-views-slot, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim: "views/ (Recommended)"): the pack folder that houses cockpit views is views/ — a ninth slot, fleet's own addition to Gas City's eight, chosen as the word VS Code (contributes.views), Obsidian (ItemView), Slack (views.publish), Raycast (root views) and Linear (custom views) share; Gas City's format has no slot for a screen, so nothing collides. title: Rename gates: the human pause is a hold, its answer a clearance, and automated pass/fail conditions are checks
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, raised while reading core/src/store.rs:206-224. Alberto, verbatim:
"gates. same thing as above. explain it to me, what it is, where it came from, why we need it. the word gate matches our flying analogies so im not opposed to keeping it i just wanna make sure that everything borrowed from beads makes sense and is well defined inside of fleet. other tools have different names for this like checks so it might be worth exploring what the canonical terms out there are"

Ruling (AskUserQuestion, 2026-09-23): adopt hold / clearance / checks. The human pause is a HOLD, its answer is a CLEARANCE, and automated pass/fail conditions are CHECKS.

Where the word comes from: bd's gate is an "async wait condition that blocks workflow steps", with types human, timer, gh:run, gh:pr and bead (`bd gate --help`, bd 1.2.2). fleet uses only `human`: fleet ask raises one (Store::gate, core/src/store.rs:206-212), the item leaves the ready set, and fleet answer resolves it (Store::resolve_gate, :223-224).

The five senses of "gate" inside fleet today (39 source files mention it), each mapped under the ruling:
1. bd's human gate, the question that parks an item: core/src/item/gate.rs and Store::gate/open_gates/resolve_gate. Becomes a HOLD; answering it is its CLEARANCE. The verbs fleet ask / fleet answer and the word "parked" already fit, and the spec pass decides whether the verbs are renamed.
2. The builder's gate, the command handed by fleet dispatch --touched (11 hits for "builder's gate"). Becomes a CHECK.
3. The landing's gate rows, each condition fleet land verifies before its push (6 hits for "gate row"). Become CHECKS.
4. The [gates] policy table (core/src/policy.rs:25-32, 71-97): ci_marker, tool_commands, release_ref_glob and the prod_* targets. These are not all checks. The spec pass names the table from what it holds.
5. The controller's routine gate, controller/src/routines/gate.rs, which decides whether a routine fires. The spec pass decides whether that is a check or a trigger condition with its own name.

Canonical terms elsewhere, from general knowledge and to be surveyed in the spec pass: automated pass/fail is a "check" (GitHub status checks, the Checks API) or a "quality gate" (SonarQube, Azure Pipelines release gates); a human pause is an "approval" (GitHub environments, GitLab), a "manual judgment" (Spinnaker), an "input" (Jenkins), a "suspend" (Argo) or an "interrupt" (LangGraph).

Scope: code identifiers, user-facing text, docs/ (docs/items.md, docs/guards.md and others), the pack's templates and skills, and the event names (gate.resolved, and so on). The bd adapter keeps bd's own word internally (fleet-0q4).

Acceptance: no user-facing surface uses "gate" for a fleet concept. The suites beside the touched files are green, and the event-name change is listed on the bead for anything that reads the stream.

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed.

description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, raised while reading core/src/store.rs:143-242. Alberto, verbatim:
"seats. i keep seeing it mentioned everywhere. explain it to me, what it is, where it came from, why we need it. if it's what i think it is, a string that is meant to represent a human or agent then i have follow-ups: the id of a seat cant be the name, the name should be optional and seat id should be a short id from the uuid crate. earlier you asked me that we need to ask the user for a name during create so that assigned_by can use it. we shouldnt have to ask the user that. during create the human should get an autogenerated uuid and an entry on fleet.toml with name empty, they can add their name if they want. later on if we have things like a cloud offering and workspaces, etc. those seats and their ids should carry over. a seat should also say whether it's a human or an agent."

Rulings (AskUserQuestion, 2026-09-23):
- A seat's id is a full UUID v7, stored whole and displayed as a short prefix. Every command that takes a seat accepts the id, any unique prefix of it, or a unique name. Rationale: a truncated id is unique within one fleet only, and seats carry over into future workspaces.
- A seat has an optional name and a kind: human or agent.
- A human's seat is a MACHINE IDENTITY plus a PROJECT ROW. Each machine keeps "who I am" (id, kind human, optional name) in the machine directory. The project's fleet.toml lists seats by id. A new collaborator's first command creates their machine identity and offers to add it to the project. Nobody is asked for a name.

Today, at primary 0f8ad4c:
- A seat is an agent slot: a seat-list row in <machine dir>/config.json, a worktree, and a session the controller keeps alive (brain/fleet-vision.md:29-30; docs/seats.md, Terms).
- Named seats are [seats.<name>] in fleet.toml, keyed by name, with chosen_name as a display name (docs/seats.md:40-60). Transient seats are named transient-<n>.
- Humans are not seats. They are a free-string actor: --by, or FLEET_ACTOR / BEADS_ACTOR (cli/src/item.rs:1165-1175), written into bd's audit trail and every note.
- The name is the id. core/src/lib.rs:90-97: retire must withdraw every order a seat holds because the next spawn takes the lowest free transient-<n> and would inherit a standing order. A unique id removes that class of bug.

Constraints for the design pass:
- core carries only serde, serde_json and toml (core/Cargo.toml:18-29). Adding `uuid` is Alberto's ruling above; the manifest comment is updated with the reason.
- Everything keyed by seat name today moves to the id: the seat list, worktree and session names, the assignee and orders.seat (fleet-0q4's SeatName becomes SeatId), --to, and fleet seat retire.
- The actor (`by`) becomes a seat id, so a human's acts carry their seat.
- The controller manages agent seats only. A human seat has no session, worktree or revive.
- Migration of existing fleet.toml [seats.<name>] tables and seat-list rows: the spec pass decides, given release/0.1.0 is not yet out.

Related: fleet-0q4 (SeatName → SeatId in the domain types), fleet-zlk (assignee vs orders.seat).

Acceptance: a design note on this bead ruled by Alberto, then implementation beads split from it.

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is designed and specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed.
notes: DECISION (fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23): CLEAN BREAK before 0.1.0. No migration of [seats.<name>] tables or seat-list rows; this repo's fleet.toml and machine directory are converted once by hand in the landing.

title: Adopt an existing board: a read-only scan verb and a mapping skill for projects adding fleet
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23. Raised by Alberto, verbatim: "we're gonna need either a verb or an agent skill that helps users normalize data if they're adding fleet to an existing project. if the user wants to fly beads that use different conventions wouldnt the tool throw an error? for example if the existing beads were using metadata.orders but with slightly different schema"

Fence: none. No verb, doc or skill covers adopting an existing board today: `git grep -n -i 'adopt\|existing project\|existing board\|onboard' -- docs cli/src/main.rs` finds nothing.

Shape (recommended in the sitting, Alberto chose to file it as two parts under one bead):
1. A READ-ONLY VERB, which measures. It scans the project's board and reports, with counts and example ids:
   - items carrying names fleet owns but did not write (after fleet-4j6, anything under the `fleet` key or `fleet:` labels that fails fleet's schema);
   - foreign conventions a person may want mapped into fleet's: an existing order-like metadata key, an existing notion of assignee or reviewer, and labels or types the project's rules would need to match;
   - notes carrying fleet's marker words, until fleet-zlk retires the prose grammar.
   It writes nothing. It uses the shared exit codes: 0 means nothing to adopt, 1 means found and listed, 3 means the board could not be read. Candidate homes are `fleet adopt --check` or a check in the defaults' doctor slot; the spec pass picks one.
2. A SKILL, which applies judgement. It walks a person through the verb's report: what each foreign convention means, how it maps onto fleet's (for example "your orders.owner is our seat"), and the migration writes, each one confirmed by the person before it is made and read back after.

Depends on fleet-4j6: until fleet's own keys are namespaced, "foreign" and "fleet's" cannot be told apart on the board.

Acceptance: the verb's suite drives a fixture board with a foreign metadata.orders, a `run` label that is not fleet's, and marker words in a person's note, and the report names each one. The skill is exercised once against that fixture board, and the transcript is on the bead.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed.

title: Namespace what fleet owns on the board: its metadata keys and the run label collide with an existing board's data
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, core/src/store.rs:360-381 and core/src/item/run.rs:88. Raised by Alberto, verbatim: "if the user wants to fly beads that use different conventions wouldnt the tool throw an error? for example if the existing beads were using metadata.orders but with slightly different schema"

F [Required] correctness core/src/item/run.rs:88, core/src/store.rs:360-381 — fleet claims plain names in shared spaces: the metadata keys `orders`, `flight` and `run`, and the label `run`. On a board that already uses any of them, fleet refuses, misreads silently, or acts on the user's data.

Fence: none cited for the plain names. store.rs:181-188 explains ONE WRITER PER TOP-LEVEL KEY because bd merges metadata at the top level. A single namespaced key keeps that property: fleet owns one key and nobody else writes it.

Evidence, at primary 0f8ad4c, by reading (no failing test yet):
- Refuses: dispatch refuses any item with a foreign metadata.orders of any shape, as "already carries an order" (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:189-195).
- Misreads: orders_of reads each field as a string and silently turns a number or an object into None (store.rs:370).
- Acts on the user's data, retire: seat::retire::held takes every open item assigned to the seat that has an `orders` key (core/src/seat/retire.rs:40-47) and withdraws it, clearing the assignee and unsetting metadata.orders. If a seat's name matches an existing assignee, the user's own metadata.orders is deleted.
- Acts on the user's data, the run label: the bare label `run` (run.rs:88) marks a run's record item. gate::ask treats such an item as a run's park, which "touches no git at all" (core/src/item/gate.rs:127-133). A seat on an existing item labelled `run` that asks a question has its work left uncommitted before it is retired. land.rs:1752-1765 uses the same label to decide whether the landing acts as the reviewer.

Remedy:
- Fleet writes and reads ONE metadata key it owns, `fleet`, carrying a schema number and holding `orders`, `run` and anything later beneath it.
- Fleet's run records carry a namespaced label, `fleet:run` (or the kind fleet-zlk settles).
- A read that finds no `fleet` key reads "no order", whatever else the item's metadata holds.
- A `fleet` key with a schema this binary does not know is exit 3, could not tell, never a guess.
- metadata.flight has no reader (held finding F1 on fleet-alt.1) and is not carried over.
- The note marker words are fleet-zlk's.

Acceptance, suites beside the touched files on the fake store:
- An item with a foreign metadata.orders (any shape) dispatches normally, and its foreign key is untouched after dispatch, deliver, retire and land.
- An item labelled `run` that is not a fleet run record asks, parks and commits like any other item.
- Existing fleet-written records keep working, or a one-time migration is part of this bead: the spec pass decides which, given release/0.1.0 is not yet out.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

Related: fleet-0q4 (the adapter owns the storage layout), fleet-zlk (typed record; note markers).

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed.
notes:
DECISION (fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23): CLEAN BREAK before 0.1.0. No migration code; the namespaced shapes are the only shapes; this repo's own board is converted once by hand in the landing.
FOLDED IN (fleet-alt.1 store sweep, 2026-09-23, Alberto): fleet-y3l. Its ACs become this bead's: (AC-y1) dispatch's RERUN line is chosen per disagreeing field: assignee gives the assignee repair, the index gives the namespaced-key repair; (AC-y2) the wrong-assignee arm asserts the assignee repair and is shown red first (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:727-735; core/tests/dispatch.rs:552). ALSO IN SCOPE: packs/tiny/skills/preboard/SKILL.md:47 (filter 5) reads the bare  key and must read fleet's namespaced one; docs/items.md:22,87 name metadata.orders.
CORRECTION to the note above (a shell quoting slip dropped a word): "reads the bare  key" should read "reads the bare orders key". packs/tiny/skills/preboard/SKILL.md:47 (filter 5) treats an orders key on the item as ASSIGNED, and must read fleet's namespaced key instead.

title: Design: an item's record is a timeline of typed entries the store adapter owns, not prose notes parsed back
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, raised by Alberto while reading core/src/store.rs:24-66, verbatim:
"why do we need to also show it in notes for a human? that's making an assumption based on beads being the first store adapter. whatever tool humans are using to look at items should handle reading metadata.orders and presenting that information to the user. what else is notes used for on the fleet side? right now based on just the orders case it feels like a timeline of events"

Ruling (Alberto): the record must not assume bd. A human-facing copy of structured data is the viewer's job, not the verbs'.

Fence: docs/items.md:8-10, "every verb that writes, writes a note on the item and reads it back before it exits 0, so the item's notes, in order, are its record". Its reason, one inspectable record written and read back, still holds. The medium it names (prose notes on a bd item, parsed with a marker grammar) is what this redesign replaces.

Evidence, at primary 0f8ad4c:
- Every verb that writes appends a note opened by a column-zero marker, with a grammar from a pack-overridable template in core/defaults/assets/:
  - order and withdrawal: core/src/item/dispatch.rs:419, 446 and 478; core/src/seat/retire.rs:66
  - DELIVERED / RE-DELIVERED: core/src/item/deliver.rs:172, markers at core/src/item/mod.rs:552
  - ACCEPTED / RETURNED WITH FINDINGS: core/src/item/review.rs:467, mod.rs:557
  - QUESTION and PARKED: core/src/item/gate.rs:181 and 418, markers at gate.rs:70 and mod.rs:569
  - ANSWERED: gate.rs:537, mod.rs:575
  - LANDED: core/src/item/land.rs:914, mod.rs:563
- State is decided by parsing that text back with last_region (mod.rs:593) and last_marker_at (mod.rs:666):
  - the commit to land: land.rs:567
  - the licence to squash, the last verdict naming the commit: land.rs:1682
  - the last landing: land.rs:1568
  - the last answer: land.rs:1776
  - the review's delivery: review.rs:501
  - the park's gate id: gate.rs:485
  - whether a park is answered, by marker order: gate.rs:659-665
  - the last verdict: gate.rs:736
- Only the order keeps a structured copy (metadata.orders); every other entry kind exists only as prose.
- The same moments are also written, typed, to the controller's event stream (item.dispatched, item.landed, …), so there are two timelines.
- Guarding against quoted markers is its own code: mod.rs:586-592.

Direction (for the design pass, not a spec):
- The store keeps an item's timeline as typed entries: a kind, structured fields (commit, verdict, gate id, seat, ordinal …) and any human-authored body (findings, a question's options) as a field.
- Current state is a fold over typed entries, never a parse of text.
- The order note goes away; the order is an entry or the index.
- Presentation is the viewer's.
- The bd adapter (fleet-0q4) chooses how entries are stored.
- To settle in design: whether the item timeline and the event stream become one log or stay two; what happens to the pack-overridable note templates; how docs/items.md restates "the record".

Related: fleet-0q4 (the adapter this sits behind). fleet-nv0 (brief decides from the index) stands on its own and can land first.

Acceptance: a design note on this bead, ruled by Alberto, then implementation beads split from it.
Gate line: per implementation bead.

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is designed and specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed.
notes:
DESIGN QUESTIONS ADDED from walkthrough fleet-alt.1: (1) labels as a kind: gate.rs:132 and land.rs:1758 recognise a run's record item by a label; a typed record would name the kind. (2) assignee duplicates orders.seat on an ordered item, and dispatch writes and checks both (dispatch.rs:547); decide whether the assignee is its own fact or the adapter's rendering of the order.
DECISION (fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23): one log or two (the item timeline vs the event stream) is decided IN THE DESIGN PASS, which compares both with a worked example; Alberto rules there.
CASES THE DESIGN MUST MAKE IMPOSSIBLE (held here, fleet-alt.1 store sweep): fleet-4rl (a second column-zero marker in a note body is read as a new region, deliver.rs:404-427 / mod.rs last_region); fleet-20s (preboard reads an 'On flight' note nothing writes); fleet-56e (landing records carry 7-char shas beside full ones); fleet-z4w (the SDK's gate park and the crash-cap park both write item.parked, and the controller's fold cannot tell them apart).

title: fleet brief decides from the order index, not a text search of the notes
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, core/src/item/brief.rs:146-153 and :268-274, raised by Alberto: "isnt searching the notes for orders given really brittle? isnt that what beads metadata is for?"

F [Required] correctness core/src/item/brief.rs:268-274 — `fleet brief` gates on order_line(), the last line anywhere in the notes containing "orders given" (brief.rs:146-153). A withdrawn order still passes, so a brief goes out for an item nobody holds, which brief.rs:255-257 says must never happen.

Fence: brief.rs:255-257, "a brief for it would tell a seat it may begin when nothing said so". The fence holds; the gate reads the wrong surface to enforce it. docs/items.md:21-23 defines the order as the note plus the index, and the index is the machine-read half.

Evidence, at primary 0f8ad4c, by reading (no failing test exists yet):
- Notes are append-only. A withdrawal writes "ORDER WITHDRAWN at retire" (core/src/seat/retire.rs:26) or "DISPATCH WITHDRAWN — spawn refused" (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:47), and neither contains "orders given". It also unsets metadata.orders (Store::withdraw_order).
- After a withdrawal, order_line still returns the old "dispatched by X — orders given" line, and brief::for_item (called from cli/src/item.rs:860) renders the brief.
- Every other order decision already reads the index: dispatch.rs:189, 427, 454, 558 and 712; deliver.rs:286; review.rs:396; seat/retire.rs:44 and 69.
- A person's note containing "orders given" would also be taken as the order line.

Remedy: brief::for_item refuses unless the item's index is present and readable (item.orders is Some, the same reading the other verbs take). The brief's order text is rendered from the index, or from the note only when the index agrees. order_line stays only as dispatch's read-back of its own write (dispatch.rs:589); the note is the record people read and no code decides from it.

Acceptance: a suite beside core/src/item/brief.rs (core/tests) drives three cases on the fake store: dispatch, then withdraw, then brief refuses with exit 1; a note containing "orders given" on an item with no index is refused; a dispatched item still gets its brief. The suites beside the touched files are green.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

SPEC'D in the sitting to the zero-clarification bar.
notes: AMENDED from walkthrough fleet-alt.1 (Alberto): struck the remedy's clause 'the note is the record people read'. Alberto, verbatim: 'whatever tool humans are using to look at items should handle reading metadata.orders and presenting that information to the user.' Whether an order note is written at all is decided in fleet-zlk. This bead's fix stands: fleet brief decides from metadata.orders, never from order_line.

title: Archive the PRDs for built work: the code and docs/ are the source of truth
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, raised while reading core/src/store.rs:1-22 against packs PRD principle 7.

Alberto, verbatim: "another for archiving PRDs for things that are already built. we dont need to keep updating prds as we work on stuff, the code and docs/ are the source of truth"

Fence: none cited for keeping PRDs live. The PRDs are drafts: each opens "Drafted 2026-09-0x/13, from a sitting …" (brain/prds/*.md:2).

Evidence, at primary 0f8ad4c:
- There are five PRDs under brain/prds/: fleet-bench, fleet-cli, fleet-controller, fleet-flights and fleet-packs. Bench does not look built: `git grep -n -i bench -- cli/src/main.rs` finds no verb. The spec pass confirms which PRDs are built, whole or in part (each has P1 sections that may not be).
- docs/ holds nine area files: README, conventions, getting-started, guards, items, packs, runs, seats and status.
- PRD citations in product code comments: 132 lines match `(packs|flights|controller|cli|bench) PRD` under core/src, controller/src, cli/src and packs.
- Skills that point at PRDs: .claude/skills/walkthrough/SKILL.md (§ 3 law 3 reads a fence "from its page under brain/prds/"; § 9 house rules name "the decisions in brain/prds/"), .claude/skills/docs/SKILL.md, packs/tiny/skills/report/SKILL.md and packs/tiny/skills/runbook/SKILL.md.

Remedy (direction, not spec):
- Move the built PRDs to an archive location, marked as history and no longer maintained.
- Leave any unbuilt PRD, or unbuilt part of one, where it is, or fold it into items.
- Decide what the 132 code citations become: pointers into the archive, or the constraint restated in the comment itself.
- Repoint the skills' fence source at the code and docs/.

Acceptance: no skill or doc tells a reader to consult or update a PRD for built behaviour. Every PRD citation left in code resolves to a file that exists.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed.
notes: DECISION (fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, 'Archive + restate'): built PRDs move to brain/archive/prds/, marked as history and unmaintained. Each PRD citation in product code is rewritten as the constraint itself (rule 5: a comment states a constraint the code cannot show), leaving no PRD id in product code. The spec pass lists which PRDs are built (bench appears not to be) and repoints the four skills.

title: Refactor store: isolate the work graph from beads behind an adapter, ready for new adapters
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, core/src/store.rs:1-22.

Alberto, verbatim: "Store needs to be completely isolated from beads and ready to support new adapters in the future."

Fence: packs PRD principle 7, "Beads the one dependency. The work graph is bd's; every note a verb writes is a bd note … nothing here invents a second store" (brain/prds/fleet-packs-prd.md:76-78), and R20, "A verb writes to the work graph through `bd` only; no verb reaches the store another way" (:585-586). Alberto's ruling above reverses principle 7 for the store boundary. R20's intent, that no verb goes around the store, still holds: it is what the adapter enforces.

Evidence, at primary 0f8ad4c:
- The trait and the bd adapter share one module. Store is at core/src/store.rs:143-242, Bd at :244-720, and the trait's docs cite bd behaviour ("measured on bd 1.2.2", :208-221).
- A bd path is published at the trait's level: EXPORT = ".beads/issues.jsonl" (store.rs:20-22). It is imported by core/src/item/land.rs:54, which also knows the .beads/ directory (land.rs:614, 649-671, 720, 2015-2030).
- Files outside store.rs and test_support.rs that mention bd or beads (git grep -c -i 'beads\|\bbd\b'): cli/src/item.rs 28, core/src/item/land.rs 11, cli/src/runs.rs 8, cli/src/transient.rs 4, cli/src/prime.rs 4, core/src/item/run.rs 3, controller/src/routines/action.rs 3, core/src/item/review.rs 2, core/src/item/dispatch.rs 2, core/src/item/deliver.rs 2, and one each in core/src/guard/mod.rs, controller/src/lifecycle.rs, cli/src/step.rs, cli/src/status.rs and cli/src/main.rs. Some of these are prose and some are behaviour, such as a RERUN line printing a bd command (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:487) or bd binary resolution (cli/src/runs.rs:56-63). The spec pass sorts which is which.

Remedy (direction, not spec):
- The store module holds the trait and its domain types, with no bd vocabulary.
- The bd adapter becomes its own module.
- Every bd fact moves behind the adapter: the argv, the quirks, the export file and the directory it lives in, and the binary resolution.
- Verbs and the cli reach the store only through the trait.
- Whatever the landing must commit into git (today the export) comes from the adapter, not from a constant.

Acceptance: behaviour preserved. No file outside the adapter names bd or .beads in code. The suites beside the touched files are green.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed. It likely exceeds 500 lines, so the spec pass splits it: the adapter module first, then each leaking caller.
notes:
SCOPE ADDED from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23 (Alberto chose 'fold into fleet-0q4'): the adapter's trait speaks in domain types, not bd strings. (1) A Status enum with a catch-all variant for a status the store answers and fleet does not know. Evidence: status is compared to string literals at core/src/item/deliver.rs:318, core/src/item/dispatch.rs:215 and :702, core/src/item/land.rs:522 and :991, core/src/item/run.rs:386, :565 and :597 (through a private CLOSED const at run.rs:100), core/src/store.rs:395, and cli/src/prime.rs:257 (raw JSON). (2) Newtypes ItemId, GateId, SeatName and Actor. Evidence: assign(item, seat, by), note(item, text, by), gate(item, reason, by) and close(item, reason, by) each take several &str in a row, with 46 call sites of the Store write/read methods outside store.rs; resolve_gate(gate, by) accepts an item id silently. item_type STAYS a string: its one reader, core/src/item/rules.rs:111, compares it with a type the project writes in [[core.flight.rules]], so the set of types is the project's.
FROM fleet-alt.1 (Alberto's question on orders): an order is a fleet concept laid onto bd's generic assignee, notes and metadata (docs/items.md:21-23; core/defaults/assets/dispatch-note.md; core/src/item/brief.rs:34-36). The adapter's trait should offer order operations (write this order, withdraw it) rather than set_metadata/unset_orders, and let each adapter decide how an order is stored.
SCOPE ADDED from walkthrough fleet-alt.1 (Alberto chose 'fold into fleet-0q4'): the domain Item type. (a) orders + has_orders_key (store.rs:40,44) become one three-variant enum (none / unreadable / an order), so the impossible Some-with-false state cannot be built; Orders.kind becomes an enum of dispatch and review (dispatch.rs:31,37); the other Orders fields become typed (Actor, SeatName, a timestamp). (b) assignee (store.rs:37) becomes Option<SeatName>. (c) run (store.rs:59, free JSON) becomes a typed record owned by the run module; its reader run.rs:392-410 fetches keys by name today. (d) document (store.rs:65, bd's raw JSON as text) moves inside the adapter: the negative control (dispatch.rs:603 and five siblings) checks the adapter's read, not the domain. created_at and flight are dead and held as findings on fleet-alt.1, not part of this scope.
SCOPE ADDED from walkthrough fleet-alt.1 (Alberto chose 'fold into fleet-0q4'): the reads. ready (store.rs:146), open_labelled (:155) and assigned_to (:172) collapse into one list(&Filter) -> Vec<ItemSummary>, where the filter is open-and-unblocked / open-with-label / assigned-to-seat and a summary carries id, status, labels and order state. show stays. show_text goes with fleet-zlk (rendering is the viewer's). open_gates stays separate: it lists another object, renamed under fleet-6gr. A single query(enum) was argued against and not taken: six different return types would need either an enum result with impossible arms or a generic method that &dyn Store cannot call. Also: SeatName becomes SeatId under fleet-iex.
DESIGN INPUT from walkthrough fleet-alt.1 (2026-09-23): beads v1.3.0 (2026-09-15) ships bd serve, an HTTP API of 41 OpenAPI-specified operations (internal/httpapi/spec/openapi.v0.yaml) with typed errors and work leases; this machine runs bd 1.2.2. The bd adapter could talk to bd serve instead of spawning bd per call. This lines up with brain/fleet-layers.md:62-76 (ruled 2026-09-17: the adapter is an executable with JSON in and out, checked by fleet store check). Wire types: fleet-xie. Also, docs/reference/json-schema.md in beads says status is 'not a closed vocabulary' (custom statuses), which confirms the Status enum's catch-all.
DECISION (fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, AskUserQuestion, after Alberto asked what the end result looks like): END STATE = the executable store contract (brain/fleet-layers.md:601-610, Q1 and Q2 ruled 2026-09-17), with the bd adapter COMPILED IN. (1) A written contract: fixed verbs, JSON in and out, fleet's exit table, schema_version on every response, and semantics defined by the contract (ready and its order, metadata writes, holds). Request and response types are fleet's domain types. (2) Core's Store trait keeps one production implementation, the contract client; the test fake stays. (3) The bd adapter (today's Bd plus fleet-ah4/9r6/fhi/xie/4j6) implements the contract in-process: no extra process on the default path. External adapters are executables named in fleet.toml ([store] adapter = "bd" | <path>). (4) fleet store check [--adapter <path>] runs a conformance suite on a scratch store, and the built-in bd adapter is checked by the same suite. This moves the executable contract ahead of the post-MVP order in fleet-layers.md:583-589, at Alberto's ruling. Transport inside the bd adapter stays the CLI per call; bd serve is a later adapter change. SEQUENCING: fleet-ah4, fleet-9r6, fleet-fhi first (the adapter's insides); fleet-zlk and fleet-iex settle before the contract's verbs and types are fixed. The spec pass splits this bead into: the contract doc and types; the adapter move; adapter selection; fleet store check.
FROM the store sweep (fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23): bd knowledge the adapter must absorb that was not in the first evidence list: (a) cli/src/prime.rs:217-227, prime's own bounded bd reader (fleet-rzixz); (b) cli/src/item.rs:455, item verbs open the store by bare name; (c) repair lines that print bd commands (dispatch.rs RERUN, fleet-y3l folded into fleet-4j6) must name a fleet command or nothing once the adapter owns bd. RELATED: fleet-6ravv.4 (its 'one contract suite run against both stores' is this bead's fleet store check run against the fake and the real adapter); fleet-bk115 (tests the store opener BdStores::resolved, cli/src/runs.rs:53, which adapter selection replaces).

WALKTHROUGH — /walkthrough, 2026-09-23, with Alberto.

Scope: core/src/{lib,store,policy,lock,digest,registry,os_litter,pack,resolve,defaults,embedded,settings,add,remove}.rs, core/build.rs.
