notes:
PLAN — fleet-alt.1, core foundations, 4,696 lines, five sections in reading order (line numbers at primary 0f8ad4c):

1. The work graph boundary — core/src/lib.rs:1-129 (map only; its verbs are outline sections 3–4), core/src/store.rs:1-769. ~900 lines.
   Trace: dispatch writes the order index and reads it back — Store::set_orders → Bd::wrote → Bd::run (`bd -C <root> update <id> --metadata … --actor`) → Answer; then Store::show → first_value → sole → the error key → item_from → orders_of.
   First appearances: the Store trait as the seam a suite forces a disagreeing read-back through; "the record before the act's end" (rules.md); Missing vs Unreadable as exit 1 vs exit 3; bd as a dependency boundary (first JSON value, -n 0 caps, null-not-[] listings, top-level metadata merge).

2. The pack format — core/src/pack.rs:1-840, core/src/registry.rs:1-102, core/src/os_litter.rs:1-19. ~960 lines.
   Trace: `fleet pack check packs/tiny` — pack::check → dir_names (OS litter) → SLOTS → parse_manifest → string_key / parse_runtime (placeholders) / parse_config (declarations) → check_slots → check_registry.
   First appearances: the Gas City reference format (G24) and the one slot it lacks (workflows); the runtime table's five placeholders; a pack setting's declaration; the shadow registry.

3. Layers, and the two censuses — core/src/resolve.rs:1-472, core/src/settings.rs:1-249, core/src/policy.rs:1-226. ~950 lines.
   Trace: `fleet run takeoff` resolving its workflow and reading `takeoff.test` — resolve::layers → installed → ordered → layers_over (defaults placed at the bottom) → resolve → unlisted_shadows → slot_path; settings::resolve → set; policy::read("core.run", "max_open").
   First appearances: layering and shadowing; the bottom layer's registry as the whole shadowable surface; the census (a key nothing reads is a gate a person believes in) and MOVED.

4. The defaults and the lock — core/build.rs:1-86, core/src/embedded.rs:1-66, core/src/digest.rs:1-131, core/src/defaults.rs:1-436, core/src/lock.rs:1-222. ~940 lines.
   Trace: `fleet start` materializing the defaults — build.rs → embedded::FILES → defaults::install → lock::read → retire_bundled_core → tree_hash vs embedded_hash → swap_in → pin → lock::append / holds → lock::write (temp, sync, rename).
   First appearances: embedded-then-materialized (readers take a path); the tree hash as the ownership test; the hand-rolled SHA-256 and why; packs.lock.

5. Adding and removing a pack — core/src/add.rs:1-741, core/src/remove.rs:1-208. ~950 lines.
   Trace: `fleet pack add <checkout>//packs/tiny --version <v>` — parse_source → parse_version → Scratch → fetch (clone --no-checkout, checkout, rev-parse) → check_format → locate_import (ts Inside) → AlreadyInstalled → check_layering → rename imports first → pin; then `fleet pack remove` — importers → directory → drop_line.
   First appearances: the two-slash source form; imports installed from the same clone; the write order that leaves a recoverable state.

Sections run 900–960 lines, a little over the 800 guide, because each is one subsystem; "slower" splits the next one.
PACING (Alberto, verbatim): "we're gonna go file by file and line by line instead of this giant wall of text, at the beginning of each section it should just point at where to start. the check should happen at the end of each section to make sure i know how things work. the findings should also go at the end of each section since right now i dont have enough knowledge to make a decision. the findings should be walked one by one with AskUserQuestion" — Part 1 restarts at core/src/store.rs:1 in small line-range steps; the part-1 check posted earlier is withdrawn and asked again at the end of the part; F1–F3 held until then.
SKILL: .claude/skills/walkthrough/SKILL.md edited at Alberto's word ("modify the walkthrough skill based on this feedback") — § 8 file-by-file steps, the opening only points, check and tie-up trace at section end; § 10 findings one at a time via AskUserQuestion after the check; § 7, § 11 and the description aligned. Left uncommitted in the primary.
Q (Alberto): "why is there anything mentioning beads at this level?" — A: by design — packs PRD principle 7 ("Beads the one dependency … nothing here invents a second store", fleet-packs-prd.md:76-78) and R20 (:585-586); the Store trait is a test seam (store.rs:4-6), not a backend abstraction, so store.rs is the one module meant to know bd. The leak worth judging is bd knowledge past it: core/src/item/land.rs:54,614,2030 (EXPORT, .beads/) and cli/src/item.rs (28 bd mentions) — held for outline sections 4 and 10.
FILED (Alberto's word, off his question on store.rs:1-22): fleet-0q4 ← "Store needs to be completely isolated from beads and ready to support new adapters in the future. file a bead for it"; fleet-g68 ← "another for archiving PRDs for things that are already built. we dont need to keep updating prds as we work on stuff, the code and docs/ are the source of truth". Both marked FINDING, NOT A SPEC.
Q (Alberto): "why is status and item_type not an enum?" — A: no reason is written beside either; both copy bd's string. status should be an enum (11 literal comparisons across 6 files, and a typo compiles), with a catch-all variant; item_type stays a string because the project's rules config owns its values (rules.rs:111). Q (Alberto): "what's an order?" — A: the record that says a seat may begin (dispatch.rs:1-11): assignee, order note and metadata.orders index, written as one act, note before index; it exists for rule 1, work is given never taken; kind is dispatch or review (dispatch.rs:31,37). Q (Alberto): "would it make sense to wrap id string in a newtype?" — A: yes; the trait takes several &str in a row (assign(item, seat, by) etc., 46 call sites), and gate ids and item ids are interchangeable today. DECISION: folded both into fleet-0q4 (AskUserQuestion).
Q (Alberto): "lets talk more about orders, is it like a special kind of bead? did we define it or is it something beads already defines?" — A: fleet defines it; bd has no notion of an order. An order is a convention stored in three generic bd places: the assignee field, a note ending in 'orders given' (template core/defaults/assets/dispatch-note.md, found by ORDER_MARK at core/src/item/brief.rs:34-36), and a metadata key 'orders' (by, kind, seat, at, ordinal). Definition: docs/items.md:21-23. The note is the record a person reads; the index is the machine-readable copy so no verb parses prose.
Q (Alberto): "isnt searching the notes for orders given really brittle? isnt that what beads metadata is for?" — A: yes. Every decision already reads the index except brief::for_item (brief.rs:269), which gates on order_line's text search; a withdrawn order leaves the old 'orders given' line behind, so fleet brief renders for an item nobody holds. FILED: fleet-nv0 (bug, SPEC'D) at Alberto's choice 'file a bug now'.
Q (Alberto): "why do we need to also show it in notes for a human? that's making an assumption based on beads being the first store adapter. whatever tool humans are using to look at items should handle reading metadata.orders and presenting that information to the user. what else is notes used for on the fleet side? right now based on just the orders case it feels like a timeline of events" — A: yes. Notes are an append-only per-item event log with marker grammars (DELIVERED, verdict, QUESTION/PARKED, ANSWERED, LANDED, plus orders), and fleet reads its state back by parsing it: land's commit and licence (land.rs:567, 1682), review's delivery (review.rs:501), the park's gate and answered-ness (gate.rs:485, 659-665). Only orders also keep a structured copy. FILED: fleet-zlk (design: typed timeline entries the adapter owns); fleet-nv0 amended.
Q (Alberto): "what other fields in Item now dont pass the smell test based on this conversation? for example, why isnt created_at a DateTime" — A: created_at is a String because core carries only serde/serde_json/toml (core/Cargo.toml:18-29) and jiff is the controller's, but nothing reads it (F1), so delete rather than type it. Field verdicts: id → ItemId; status → enum; assignee → SeatName, and it duplicates orders.seat; notes → fleet-zlk; orders+has_orders_key → one enum; blockers → Vec<ItemId>; item_type stays; labels used as a run-record kind tag (gate.rs:132, land.rs:1758); flight DEAD (no reader; its intended consumer rules::effective at core/src/item/rules.rs:58 has no caller anywhere); run → typed record; document → inside the adapter. DECISION: reshapes folded into fleet-0q4; labels-as-kind and assignee-vs-seat noted on fleet-zlk. HELD for section end: F1 widened to include Item.flight; rules::effective's dead matcher held for outline section 3.
Q (Alberto): "we're gonna need either a verb or an agent skill that helps users normalize data if they're adding fleet to an existing project. if the user wants to fly beads that use different conventions wouldnt the tool throw an error? for example if the existing beads were using metadata.orders but with slightly different schema" — A: not reliably. It refuses (dispatch.rs:189), misreads silently (store.rs:370, the note marker words), or acts on the user's data: retire unsets a foreign metadata.orders (retire.rs:40-47), and the bare label 'run' makes ask skip the git commit (gate.rs:127-133). The root cause is fleet claiming plain names in shared spaces. FILED (Alberto chose 'two beads'): fleet-4j6 (bug, namespace fleet's keys and label; Required) and fleet-0ml (read-only scan verb + mapping skill; blocked by fleet-4j6).
Q (Alberto): "for Ready why not ReadyItem, Ready made me think it's an event or something else entirely?" — A: agreed; Row (store.rs:110-121) has the same vagueness. Ready is F1's to delete (ready() answers ids, since its one caller dispatch.rs:179-182 checks membership only); if kept, rename it ReadyItem. HELD F4 [Nit] readability core/src/store.rs:110-121 — Row names neither its listing nor its subject — remedy: rename to AssignedItem; read by core/src/seat/retire.rs:40-47 and core/src/item/deliver.rs:286.
HELD F5 [Optional] architecture core/src/item/{brief,deliver,dispatch,gate,land,review,run}.rs — the StoreError→Stop mapping (Missing→refused/exit 1, Unreadable→could_not_tell/exit 3) is written 8 times across 7 files, twice in dispatch.rs:687-699 alone — evidence: git grep -n 'StoreError::Missing(why) => Stop::refused' counts 8 — remedy: one From<StoreError> for Stop beside Stop in core/src/item/mod.rs, callers use ?; ≈ -40 lines
CADENCE (Alberto, verbatim, 2026-09-23): "we're gonna stop the walkthrough after this one file to work on every bead that will come out of it. that way when i review the code my knowledge of it is fresh. we will do that multiple times in the walkthrough (sometimes after one single large file like this one or maybe after 2-3 small ones) so make sure everything is being recorded on the walkthrough bead 'cause this is gonna take a week at least with many refactors along the way." — The walk pauses at a WORK BREAK after a file or a few, the beads filed off it are worked, then the walk resumes. Refactors move line numbers, so every resumption re-runs step 0 and re-plans the remaining steps against the new SHA. The first break is after core/src/store.rs.
HELD F6 [Nit] correctness core/src/store.rs:152-154 — open_labelled's doc says 'the list read answers no metadata, so a caller that needs an item's flight object reads it with Store::show'; measured on bd 1.2.2, 'bd list --label fleet --json -n 0 --all' answers fleet-6ravv WITH metadata.orders, and Row (store.rs:115-117) relies on exactly that; 'flight' is dead (F1) — remedy: drop the false sentence and the flight reference; ≈ -3 lines
Q (Alberto, verbatim): "ok three things i wanna flag: 1. seats. i keep seeing it mentioned everywhere. explain it to me, what it is, where it came from, why we need it. if it's what i think it is, a string that is meant to represent a human or agent then i have follow-ups: the id of a seat cant be the name, the name should be optional and seat id should be a short id from the uuid crate. earlier you asked me that we need to ask the user for a name during create so that assigned_by can use it. we shouldnt have to ask the user that. during create the human should get an autogenerated uuid and an entry on fleet.toml with name empty, they can add their name if they want. later on if we have things like a cloud offering and workspaces, etc. those seats and their ids should carry over. a seat should also say whether it's a human or an agent. 2. gates. same thing as above. explain it to me, what it is, where it came from, why we need it. the word gate matches our flying analogies so im not opposed to keeping it i just wanna make sure that everything borrowed from beads makes sense and is well defined inside of fleet. other tools have different names for this like checks so it might be worth exploring what the canonical terms out there are/ 3. some of these Store functions feel like queries that could belong in a single query fn with an enum passed to it, happy to be proven wrong so argue against it you think that's the wrong move"
A:
(1) A seat today is an AGENT slot: a seat-list row, a worktree and a session the controller keeps alive (brain/fleet-vision.md:29-30; docs/seats.md terms). Named seats come from [seats.<name>]; transient seats are transient-<n>. Humans are not seats: they are a free-string actor (--by, FLEET_ACTOR/BEADS_ACTOR, cli/src/item.rs:1165-1175). A seat's id is its name, and transient names are reused, which is the hazard lib.rs:90-97 guards against (orders passed to the next holder of the name); a UUID id removes it. Adjustments: store the full UUID (v7) and display a short prefix, because a truncated id is not unique across workspaces; the uuid crate breaks core's three-crate rule (core/Cargo.toml:18-29), Alberto's call; open: where a human seat lives when fleet.toml is committed project policy and a second person never runs create.
(2) A gate is bd's async wait condition (bd gate --help: human, timer, gh:run, gh:pr, bead); fleet uses only human, for ask/answer. Inside fleet "gate" means at least five things: bd's human gate, the builder's gate (--touched), the landing's gate rows, the [gates] policy table, and controller/src/routines/gate.rs; 39 source files mention it. Canonical terms (general knowledge, to be surveyed): automated pass/fail = check or quality gate; human pause = approval, manual judgment, input, suspend, interrupt. A flying option: human pause = hold, its answer = clearance, automated conditions = checks.
(3) Argued against a single query(enum): six different return types force either an enum result with impossible arms or a generic method that &dyn Store cannot call. Counter-proposal: ready, open_labelled and assigned_to collapse into one list(&Filter) -> Vec<ItemSummary>; show stays; show_text goes with fleet-zlk; open_gates stays separate.
DECISIONS (AskUserQuestion): seat id = full UUID v7, short display; human seat = machine identity + project row; gates → hold / clearance / checks; Store reads → fold the list(&Filter) counter-proposal into fleet-0q4. FILED: fleet-iex (seat identity design), fleet-6gr (gate rename). fleet-0q4 scope note added.
HELD F7 [Optional] correctness core/src/store.rs:272-287 — Bd::run waits on bd with no bound (Command::output at :275), so a bd that hangs (a stuck dolt server, a lock) hangs the verb, a landing under the lane's lock included — evidence: no timeout on the call; the controller already bounds its own child processes with platform::run_bounded — remedy: a bounded run for store calls, whose expiry is Unreadable (exit 3); the bound and where the helper lives (core cannot depend on the controller) are for the spec
Q (Alberto): "why not reuse [std] process.rs:1317 Output instead of Answer?" — A: agreed; Answer's ok, code and status() derive from ExitStatus (success(), code(), and its Display, which also names the signal), and its strings are Output's bytes decoded. The only thing it adds is decoding once, which a small text() helper or decoding at each read covers. HELD F8 [Optional] stdlib: core/src/store.rs:302-331 — Answer duplicates std::process::Output — remedy: run() returns Output; status text from ExitStatus's Display; tail() a free fn over &Output; stdout decoded where parsed; ≈ -15 lines; refusal wording moves from 'exited 1' to 'exit status: 1' (no parser reads it); pairs with F2, same code.
Q (Alberto): "explain wrote() more, what is it used for and how is it different from run" — A: run (store.rs:272-287) never judges; it returns the whole answer whatever the status, because some reads need output on a non-zero exit (show reads bd's error object to answer Missing). wrote (:289-299) is run plus a verdict for calls whose only signal is the exit: 0 → Ok(()), else Unreadable. It has 10 callers (the writes that answer nothing); run has 9 (every read, plus create and gate, which read an id). wrote's Ok means bd exited 0, not that the record holds the write; the verb's read-back proves that (rule 3). F2 is the asymmetry: the nine run callers judge by hand.
HELD F9 [Optional] correctness core/src/store.rs:383-400 — blockers_of counts EVERY dependency that is not closed, whatever its type, but its doc says 'the dependencies that still stand between this item and a start' — evidence: bd show fleet-nv0 --json lists fleet-alt.1 (in_progress, dependency_type discovered-from), and bd ready -n 0 answers fleet-nv0 as ready; so Item.blockers holds a link that blocks nothing. Consumers: why_not_ready (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:700-708) can tell a person an item is 'blocked by' a discovered-from or related link; run.rs:575 is safe because it intersects with open gate ids — remedy: count only blocking dependency types (blocks, and whatever else bd's ready honours, measured); ≈ +2 lines
Q (Alberto): "ok so these all serde funcs? is there a more elegant way to do it or is this just the glue that all Store adapters will have to make things work" — A: they are hand traversals of serde_json::Value, not derive. Every adapter needs wire→domain glue (it lives inside the adapter under fleet-0q4), but it can be declarative. HELD F10 [Optional] shrink: core/src/store.rs:333-400, 722-769 — first_value/sole/text_field/orders_of/blockers_of/labels_of/item_from hand-walk bd's JSON — remedy: #[derive(Deserialize)] wire structs (BdIssue, BdDependency; the derive feature is already in core, lock.rs:40), an untagged enum for bd's rows-or-{error} answer, and one conversion to the domain Item; metadata stays a raw map so orders keeps its three states (has_orders_key); a mistyped field becomes Unreadable instead of silently None (a behaviour change, and the fleet-4j6 misread fixed); ≈ -40 lines; belongs with fleet-0q4.
Q (Alberto): "is this schema defined somewhere in the beads project? https://github.com/gastownhall/beads could we automate generating ours based on theirs during a substrate sync?" — A: yes, two sources: docs/reference/json-schema.md (the CLI --json contract, prose, contract-tested) and internal/httpapi/spec/openapi.v0.yaml (OpenAPI 3.0.3, hand-written source of truth for bd serve, new in v1.3.0; its Issue schema is pinned to the types.Issue the CLI prints). Generation is feasible as a tools/ script at the pinned bd tag, output committed, with a drift check. 'Substrate sync' is not a process in this repo; read as moving the bd pin. FILED: fleet-xie (Alberto chose 'file it, tied to the bd pin'); the bd serve transport idea is noted on fleet-0q4. HELD F11 [Required] correctness core/src/store.rs:333-353, 403-535, 656-686 — bd v2.0 makes the JSON envelope {schema_version, data} the default (beads docs/reference/json-schema.md, 'Timeline'); every read here expects today's bare array or object, so each breaks on that bd — remedy: set BD_JSON_ENVELOPE=1 on every call now, parse the envelope, check schema_version (warn on higher, per beads' consumer guidelines), and classify Missing by the error's code 'not_found' instead of the presence of an error key.
Q (Alberto): "a lot of code in those functions is error checking and serde which should get better with xie. wrote() get used here, anything else we can do like that for the others' error checks?" — A: yes, and this sharpens F2. HELD F2 (REVISED) [Optional] shrink: core/src/store.rs:403-686 — three helpers in wrote()'s style: answered(args) (run + exit check; 7 callers: ready, show_text, open_labelled, create, assigned_to, gate, open_gates; not show, which reads the JSON before the status); listed(args) (answered + first value + require an array, null as empty for every listing; 4 callers); created_id(args) (answered + the id off the answer; create :527-534 and gate :643-653 end identically). Messages are built from the argv actually run and name self.bin, so the text can no longer drift from the call (e.g. the literal at :410 vs the argv at :407). This is the single point F11's envelope unwrapping lands in. ≈ -60 lines. ORDER: F2 helpers → F11 → fleet-xie types / fleet-0q4 list(&Filter).
HELD F12 [Required] correctness core/src/store.rs:544-569 — assigned_to runs 'bd list -a <seat> --json' with NO -n 0; bd list caps at 50 rows by default ('bd list --help': '-n, --limit int … (default 50, use 0 for unlimited)'), the very cap store.rs:474-477 names for open_labelled. Past 50 non-closed items assigned to one seat, seat::retire::held (core/src/seat/retire.rs:40-47) misses the ordered items beyond row 50, so they keep their orders when the seat's name is freed: the hazard lib.rs:90-97 says retire exists to prevent. deliver.rs:286 reads the same listing — remedy: pass -n 0, as ready/open_labelled/open_gates do; the listed() helper (F2) makes the uncapped read the only one available; +2 args
SECTION 1 (part 1 of the plan): the work graph boundary — walked core/src/store.rs:1-769 in steps (lib.rs's map deferred to outline sections 3–4). TIE-UP: dispatch writes the order index and reads it back (dispatch.rs:481-489 → store.rs:582-587 → 289-299 → 272-287 → 433-455 → 333-337 → 339-353 → 444-446 → 737-769 → 360-381 → dispatch.rs:687-692). CHECK: (1) show tests the error key before the exit status, what breaks if swapped; (2) why a failed write is Unreadable and never Missing, and what wrote's Ok does not prove; (3) why set_orders and set_metadata are two methods → Alberto: "all done" — no answers given; he moved to the findings. F10 is superseded by fleet-xie and not put to him.
FILED (findings walked one at a time, AskUserQuestion): F11 → fleet-9r6 (bug, Required, blocked by fleet-ah4); F12 → fleet-fhi (bug, Required); F2+F8 → fleet-ah4 (Alberto: file F2, fold F8 into it; blocks fleet-9r6, fleet-0q4, fleet-xie); F7 → fleet-zex (finding, not spec); F1 → fleet-16s; F5 → fleet-jqh; F9 → fleet-5y5 (bug); F3+F4+F6 → fleet-016 (one bead). F10 superseded by fleet-xie. DROPPED: none.
SPEC DECISIONS (AskUserQuestion, one at a time): bd pin → 1.3.0, checked (FILED fleet-reb, blocks fleet-xie); migration for fleet-4j6/fleet-iex → clean break before 0.1.0; fleet-0q4 → after Alberto asked for the end state ('leaning towards 3 but need more information on what the end result looks like'), the executable contract with the bd adapter compiled in plus fleet store check; fleet-zlk one log or two → decide in the design pass; fleet-6gr verbs → spec pass; fleet-g68 → brain/archive/prds/ and citations restated as constraints; fleet-zex → fixed 60s constant. Each is noted on its bead.
RESUME (WORK BREAK 1): walked core/src/store.rs:1-769 in full; the rest of section 1 of the plan (lib.rs's map) and parts 2–5 (pack format; layers and censuses; defaults and lock; add/remove) remain. Every item filed off this stretch is on departure-board.md at the repo root, in flights 1–6: fleet-ah4, fleet-fhi, fleet-jqh, fleet-nv0, fleet-9r6, fleet-16s, fleet-5y5, fleet-016, fleet-reb, fleet-xie, fleet-zlk, fleet-iex, fleet-6gr, fleet-g68, fleet-zex, fleet-4j6, fleet-0q4, fleet-0ml. Held for outline section 3: rules::effective has no caller (core/src/item/rules.rs:58). Held for sections 4 and 10: bd knowledge outside the store (land.rs EXPORT/.beads; cli/src/item.rs). Primary at 0f8ad4c. On resuming: re-run step 0; the SHA will have moved with the refactors, so the remaining plan is re-planned against the new line numbers. Uncommitted in the primary: .claude/skills/walkthrough/SKILL.md (pacing edit) and departure-board.md.
STORE SWEEP (Alberto: "flight 1 is in the air. go through all the open beads and see if there's anything in there related to the store that is either about to be stale or needs to be added to one of the flights"). 98 other non-closed beads read; 10 store-related. DECISIONS (AskUserQuestion): fleet-zex CLOSED as duplicate of fleet-rzixz (60s decision carried; rzixz takes zex's row in flight 4); fleet-ay8, fleet-998, fleet-pg7, fleet-bk115 BOARDED on flight 2 (ay8 after fleet-ah4, 998 after fleet-16s, pg7 after fleet-fhi); fleet-y3l FOLDED into fleet-4j6 and closed; fleet-4rl, fleet-20s, fleet-56e, fleet-z4w HELD FOR fleet-zlk. WALKTHROUGH OUTLINE — /walkthrough, built 2026-09-23 with Alberto.

Scope: the whole repository (.), 44,807 measured lines by the skill's pipeline; 38,584 once tests are skipped at Alberto's word ("you can skip tests") — inline #[cfg(test)] modules, core/src/test_support.rs, controller/src/test_support.rs and packs/ts/assets/sdk/testdata/ left out as well — against a ceiling of 6,000.

1. core foundations: store, policy, packs, resolve — core/src/{lib,store,policy,lock,digest,registry,os_litter,pack,resolve,defaults,embedded,settings,add,remove}.rs, core/build.rs — 4,696
2. core guard: the four pre-tool classes — core/src/guard/* — 3,028
3. core item, part 1: dispatch through gate, seat retire — core/src/item/{mod,rules,pins,brief,dispatch,deliver,review,gate}.rs, core/src/seat/* — 4,029

title: the SDK's gate parks the run's own record, and the controller's fold reads that item.parked as the crash-cap park latch, so a run that asked a gate skips its later max_crashes park
description: Found by the fleet-thh builder (2026-09-23). The SDK's gate asks through fleet ask --item <run>, which writes item.parked with item = <run>. controller/src/runs.rs fold reads an item.parked for the run as Folded.parked, the latch that says the crash-cap park already stands. So a run that asked a gate and later reaches [core.run] max_crashes is treated as already parked and gets no crash-cap gate. title: until's wake has the read-at-exit race: a delivery that lands between until's read and the workflow's exit sits at or below run.waiting's recorded seq and never wakes the run
description: Found reviewing fleet-thh (2026-09-23). run.waiting's seq is read when the workflow exits (core/src/item/run.rs read_the_exit). Wake::Items matches only item lines above that position (controller/src/runs.rs could_wake), so a line for a named item that lands after until read the stream and before exit is never matched. Matching anywhere is not safe for items because the wake does not carry which state until wants (an earlier item.dispatched would match every poll). Fix direction: carry the wanted state in the wake (the SDK throws {items, state}), then match anywhere for that state. Done when an arm with the delivery inside the gap is red, then green, and an earlier state of the same item does not re-run the workflow every poll.

description:

So `bd note x "see 6ravv"` passes the bare-id check. The tests (core/tests/guard.rs:488-535) use only `a1b2`.

title: Autopilot as a routine: a machine setting read and written through fleet settings (fleet-layers Q12, ruled A), and a routine on a schedule whose guard reads it and opens the oldest plan while the open runs are under the cap — the switch's new home after plan, fly and autopilot left core
description:
## Why

fleet-layers Q12 (ruled 2026-09-17, A): autopilot's home is a machine setting, read and written through the API, by fleet settings or the cockpit's screen — machine state, not policy, not process environment. tinytown-tnkuq.94 removed fleet autopilot and the switch file from core with plan and fly; unattended composition is tiny's takeoff workflow over fleet run (tinytown-tnkuq.110, flown). The board's line "filed when .110 has flown" is this bead. fleet-layers § What tiny ships on day one places autopilot as a routine AFTER day one, so this is not on the switch's road; it is filed so the requirement is not discoverable only by tripping over it.

## What (frame)

A settings verb (fleet settings get|set <key>) over a file in the machine directory; the key autopilot with values on and off; a routine in tiny (packs/tiny/orders or routines) on a schedule whose guard reads the setting through the API and, when on, opens the oldest plan while the open runs are under the cap ([core.run] or the routine's own cap) — never while a run is open above it; off, nothing opens. Alberto's standing order stands over it: the switch is OFF while he is asleep or absent.

## Acceptance Criteria (frame — finalized by the spec pass)

fleet settings set autopilot on|off round-trips; the routine's guard reads it; with on and no open run the oldest plan opens once; with off nothing opens; the cap holds.

## Risk

After the MVP and after the switch; owes a spec pass.

title: An end-to-end arm for the controller's run pass in the cli crate: a real scratch workflow exiting 2 then 0 driven through observe with the real Engine as the Runs seam, proving tinytown-tnkuq.105's AC1 and AC3 at the layer that can run them — the stub-seam arms measure the decision and nothing drives the three real acts
description:
## What was seen

tinytown-tnkuq.105 landed the controller's run pass (fleet/controller/src/runs.rs) as a DECISION measured against a stub seam (fleet/controller/tests/runs.rs): the stub writes what the real acts write, and every AC1-AC3 arm drives the fold and the latches that way. The three real acts — the fill of the Runs seam in fleet/cli/src/flights.rs (Engine::project_holding's walk over the registered projects, rerun over core's run::rerun with its hash-pin refusal and never-a-fresh-bundle property, the store's gate, transient::priced as the retire), and the run key on session.spawned written by transient::spawn from FLEET_RUN_ID — have no arm that drives them end to end. The reviewer verified the stub's four premises by reading the real writers (the spawn line's actor is the seat directory and the retire line's is the seat name, one string for a transient seat; the open writes hash, workflow, pack and entry into the record's run object; both crates name events.jsonl), and accepted the delivery on that reading (R2 on tinytown-f4fmz: coverage worth having, not worth a return). The reading is not a run.

## What this bead asks

One end-to-end arm in the cli crate — the member that can see both the controller and core, where fleet/cli/tests/in_process.rs already drives observe_seamed and fleet/cli/tests/run.rs already stands up a scratch pack with a stub runtime — over a real scratch project and a real workflow whose script exits 2 on its first execution and 0 on its second: fleet run opens it (run.waiting on the stream), the observe pass ticks once with a real Engine as the Runs seam and does NOT re-run it, a line is appended to the stream, the pass ticks again and run.started is counted twice, then run.closed, the record closed on the store, and run.cleaned with count 0. A second arm, or the same one extended: a seat spawned by that workflow through fleet seat spawn under FLEET_RUN_ID carries the run key on its session.spawned line and is retired by the cleanup. This is the spec's own AC1 and AC3 as written, at the layer that can run them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 the arm above, green under cd fleet and cargo nextest run -p fleet-cli filtered to it, rc 0, asserting the run.started count 1 before the appended line and 2 after, run.closed, and run.cleaned.
- AC2 a mutant that copies the recorded seq instead of taking the higher of the two (runs.rs tick's RUN_WAITING guard) reds the arm; a mutant that re-bundles instead of refusing on a moved directory (run.rs rerun's hash check) reds a second arm or a second assertion.

(fleet-test-budget-judged-under-load-condition, 2026-09-15) says the budget is
judged only when the box is under load 5, so contention never reddens a correct
tree. tinytown-6ravv.11 made `fleet-check` the FIRST step of the `fleet-test`
recipe — a good simplification — but the recipe reads the load AFTER that step,
and fleet-check runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, which compiles
every test target. So the reading is taken immediately after the recipe's own
compile and is systematically higher than the box it is meant to describe.

A reading above the ceiling is NOT JUDGED, and NOT JUDGED EXITS 0. The budget
half of the gate goes quiet rather than refusing, and quiet reads exactly like
passing. MEASURED by the operator at the landing review: 4.54 in the shell
immediately before invoking the target, 6.38 read by the recipe, verdict NOT
JUDGED on a 957-of-957 green run.

## What to build

In the `fleet-test` recipe in `Makefile`, the `load=$$(uptime ...)` assignment
moves ABOVE the `$(MAKE) -s fleet-check` line, so the reading describes the box
the run arrived on rather than the box after our own clippy. Nothing else about
the recipe changes; fleet-check stays the first gate to RUN.

Named because it is the cost of the ruling and should be stated in the delivery
rather than discovered: the reading is then stale by however long fleet-check
takes, which on a cold tree is minutes, so a run that started quiet and got busy
can still be judged. That is the tradeoff Alberto took.

## Acceptance Criteria

AC1 In `Makefile`, the `load=` assignment precedes `$(MAKE) -s fleet-check` in
    the fleet-test recipe; `git diff` quoted.
AC2 A run of `make fleet-test` on a quiet box (1-minute load under 5 measured in
    the shell first) is JUDGED rather than NOT JUDGED — the verdict line quoted
    with the shell's reading and the recipe's reading side by side, and the two
    within a stated tolerance of each other. This is the bead's whole point and
    a run that cannot show it is a RETURN, not a pass.
AC3 The NOT JUDGED path still works: with `--load-before` forced above the
    ceiling, `fleet/tools/suite-profile` still exits 0 with its NOT JUDGED line.
    (Provable without a suite run, against an existing junit.)
AC4 `make fleet-check` rc 0.

Each rc read from its own $?.

title: fleet/cli/tests/ring_flight.rs copies a template with no self-naming assertion — under the embedded board engine its copies carry the template's absolute path and nothing reports it, the silent half of tinytown-d996s
description:
fleet/cli/tests/ring_flight.rs copies a template and runs bd init in it exactly
as ring_land.rs does, and carries ZERO self-naming assertions — so under the
embedded board engine its copies carry the template's absolute path with nothing
reporting it.

FOUND while reviewing tinytown-d996s on flight tinytown-vsoep, by that bead's
builder, and confirmed by the operator as a shape rather than as a measurement.

THE SHAPE, measured: ring_flight.rs has 8 bd invocations, 4 copy_tree calls and
4 rebased() calls, and `grep -c names_itself_nowhere` returns 0. ring_land.rs,
where the defect was proven and fixed at tinytown-d996s, has all four.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY THE SAME BUG. tinytown-d996s's mechanism is that with
FLEET_TEST_DOLT_PORT unset, bd init falls back to embedded dolt and records the
git origin it finds — the template's own absolute bare — as a dolt remote in
.beads/embeddeddolt/fx/.dolt/repo_state.json. ring_land.rs FAILED LOUDLY because
its names_itself_nowhere_a_copy_would_carry assertion reads every copied file and
refuses a template path. ring_flight.rs has no such assertion, so the same
condition is SILENT there: the copies would carry the path and every arm would
pass.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the operator's attempt to establish it cheaply
FAILED BLIND, which is why this is a bead and not a hunk. Inspecting leftover
templates under the box's temp directory returned zero embeddeddolt directories
for ring_flight AND zero for the land template where the defect is proven — a
control agreeing with its subject, so the reading is evidence of nothing. The
leftovers on that box are from served runs, which write no embedded dolt at all.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one bare `cargo nextest run -P ring --test ring_flight`
(no tools/dolt-test-server, so FLEET_TEST_DOLT_PORT is unset), then a grep of the
surviving rig copies for the template's absolute path. Seven arms at 90-250 s
each on the measurements from flight tinytown-vsoep, so roughly 15-20 minutes.

WHAT TO BUILD IF IT IS REAL: the same treatment tinytown-d996s landed — a
repo_state() path helper and a rebased_if_there() call in the template build and
in the per-rig copy — AND a names_itself_nowhere assertion for ring_flight, which
is the half that makes the fix provable instead of cover. Without the assertion
there is nothing to red-prove against and the change could not be verified, which
is exactly why the operator declined to fold it into tinytown-d996s's landing
during the flight.

Not urgent: nothing is red today, because nothing looks.

title: fleet/tools/lessons-check's boundary scans only git-tracked files, so a bead id in an unstaged new file under fleet/ reads as clean and a positive control for the boundary cannot fail
description:
fleet/tools/lessons-check's boundary refuses the tinytown bead-id string under fleet/, but it only ever looks at git-TRACKED files. A builder who adds a new file under fleet/ gets a false clean until the file is staged, and the gate then fires later -- at a landing, or on someone else's run.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE by the operator, on base a78a5cc4590f: line 208 iterates tracked(root, "fleet"), and tracked() at line 60 shells out to git ls-files -- with a docstring saying git and not a walk, deliberately, because a build writes files a walk would pick up. So the choice is considered; the consequence is not.

HOW IT SURFACED. tinytown-ul822's builder wrote a positive control for the boundary -- a bead id in a new file under fleet/ -- and the control PASSED, silently, because the file was unstaged. It only fired after git add. A control that cannot fail is the failure mode this whole flight kept turning up, and here the gate itself supplies it.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The house comment rule asks for a bead pointer when the full story matters; the fleet boundary refuses exactly that string under fleet/. Builders therefore hit this constantly -- 28 sites across 10 beads on flight tinytown-tjgr7 alone -- and the one instrument that would tell them early is blind until staging.

POSSIBLE SHAPES, not a decision. Scan the working tree as well as the index for untracked candidates; or have the tool say out loud how many files it scanned and that untracked ones are excluded, so a zero-finding run states its population. The second is cheaper and is the fix this flight's evidence actually supports: the defect is a silent population, not a wrong one.
notes:
READ AGAINST ALBERTO'S D5 RULING on flight tinytown-tjgr7, 2026-09-17, by the operator who filed this bead.

His ruling on D5 (tinytown-gq0t9) adopted C: 'Dont do anything about this that will increase the time it takes to land things. we will do a comment cleanup pass and a full walkthrough once fleet migrates to its own repo'.

THE OPERATOR READS THAT AS COVERING THIS BEAD, and is saying so rather than leaving a bead sitting ready that contradicts a ruling made hours earlier. This bead is about the same instrument and the same class: lessons-check's boundary over fleet/. It is therefore DEFERRED BEHIND THE FLEET MIGRATION, to be handled by the comment cleanup pass and walkthrough his ruling names, rather than worked as its own bead now.

THE ONE REASON THAT READING MIGHT BE WRONG, stated so he can overturn it in a word: this bead's cheaper option (B) -- have lessons-check print how many files it scanned and that untracked ones are excluded, so a zero-finding run states its population -- is a DIAGNOSTIC and adds nothing to landing time, because lessons-check does not run in the landing path at all. So it is not literally caught by 'anything that will increase the time it takes to land things'. It is caught by the second half, the one-time sweep at the migration. If he wants the one-line population print before then, that is a yes on this bead and nothing else changes.

WHAT STAYS TRUE REGARDLESS, since it is a measurement and not a proposal: the boundary reads only git-tracked files, so a bead id in an unstaged new file under fleet/ is invisible to it and a positive control written that way cannot fail. Anyone writing such a control before the migration should git add the fixture first, or it will pass for the wrong reason.

title: the fleet test fixtures are not hermetic against a person's global git excludes file — GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null leaves core.excludesFile at its default, so the box's ignore file reaches the fixture
description:
## Why

The fleet test fixtures are not hermetic against the person's global git excludes file, measured on tinytown-tnkuq.69.

The suites' git helper sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, which looks like isolation and is not: it leaves `core.excludesFile` at its DEFAULT rather than empty, so the box's own global ignore file reaches the fixture. On tinytown-tnkuq.69 that made a fixture unable to track `.claude/settings.local.json` with a plain `git add` — measured failure, "The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files" — and the builder worked around it with `add --force`, which is the truthful shape for that arm but does not fix the class.

Why it matters more than today's symptom: a fixture whose behaviour depends on a file OUTSIDE the repository fails differently on different machines, and passes on the machine of whoever wrote it. That is the worst shape a test defect takes, because it is invisible to the person best placed to fix it. Today it bites one arm that tracks an ignored path; tomorrow it is any fixture whose paths some contributor's global ignore happens to name.

## What lands

1. The suites' `git_at` helpers (and any sibling that builds a fixture repo) pass `-c core.excludesFile=/dev/null` alongside the existing `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, so the fixture sees no excludes file at all.
2. A census: every helper in the fleet suites that constructs a git command, with the count examined beside the count changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 an arm that tracks a path named by a global ignore file succeeds WITHOUT `--force`. Red-prove it: with the excludesFile flag removed and a global ignore naming that path, the arm fails; the mutant must be the real helper, not a copy.
- AC2 the census's two counts quoted on the bead.
- AC3 the fleet suites green under `cargo nextest run`, counts printed before and after.
notes:
ALBERTO'S RULING on flight tinytown-tjgr7's decision log, 2026-09-17: D9 ADOPTED A, the operator's recommendation -- fly it on the next flight. Verbatim from the log: 'D9: A'. Option B (wait until it actually causes a false verdict) NOT taken. READ THIS AGAINST HIS D8, which is the same recommendation on the neighbouring bead and which he did NOT adopt: he deferred fleet-28z33 behind the fleet migration because it is documentation about how we work, which the migration will rewrite anyway, and he is flying THIS one because test hermeticity survives the migration unchanged. The operator had bundled the two as one prose item on the manifest; he split them, and split them on that line. WHAT THIS BEAD IS: the fixtures set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to /dev/null but core.excludesFile keeps its default, so a person's own global git ignore file reaches the fixture and a suite can pass on one machine and fail on another for a reason no test names. Re-measure that before building on it -- it is a reading taken 2026-09-17.

Re-measured on this box and still live. 0 test sites pass core.excludesFile; about 23 sites across 16 files set only GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null; ~/.config/git/ignore line 1 is **/.claude/settings.local.json; the --force workaround is at controller/tests/transient.rs:227-231. D9:A stands.

title: packs/tiny's handoff and clock-out skills tell a transient seat that deliver commits the staged set — tinytown-nxoqe made that false, and these are the documents a seat reads as its instructions
description:
## Why

tinytown-nxoqe landed at fb99cb6e8 and changed what `fleet deliver` does: a clean tree whose HEAD is already ahead of the item's base now delivers that HEAD as-is, committing nothing, and prints `DELIVERED AS-IS … this verb committed nothing`. A clean tree AT the base is still refused.

Two shipped skill documents still describe the old behaviour: `packs/tiny/skills/handoff/SKILL.md` and `packs/tiny/skills/clock-out/SKILL.md` both say deliver "commits the staged set". That is now false, and these are documents a transient seat READS AS ITS INSTRUCTIONS — a seat that believes it must stage something before delivering will manufacture a change, or will read the as-is delivery as a failure.

tinytown-nxoqe's builder found this and correctly declined to take it: the packs tree was outside its READY boundaries. It is filed rather than folded in because the fix belongs to the pack, not to the verb.

## What lands

1. Both SKILL.md files describe deliver's behaviour as it now is: the staged set when there is one; a clean tree ahead of the base delivered as-is; a clean tree at the base refused, with the refusal naming the way out.
2. A grep of `packs/` for any other sentence describing deliver's staging contract, with the count of files examined quoted beside the count changed — a sweep with no denominator is an assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 neither file says deliver commits the staged set unconditionally; both name the as-is case. Quoted.
- AC2 the sweep's two counts (examined, changed) quoted on the bead.
- AC3 the touched doc suites green.
notes:
ALBERTO ON flight tinytown-tjgr7's decision log, 2026-09-17: D8 MARKED (unanswered), WITH AN INSTRUCTION ATTACHED. Both halves are recorded, because they are different things and collapsing them would misreport him.

Verbatim from the log: 'D8: (unanswered) - dont do anything about this. we're gonna change everything about how we work when fleet is up and running'

THE DECISION IS NOT MADE. Per the flight-report skill, (unanswered) is not a ruling, so neither option on this card was adopted: he did not choose "fly it on the next flight" and he did not choose "fold it into the next bead that touches those skills". This bead's question -- when to correct the two skills -- remains open on the record.

THE INSTRUCTION IS CLEAR AND IS ACTED ON. Do nothing about it now. The reason he gives is that the way we work is itself about to change once fleet is running, which makes correcting documents that describe the current way of working work that may be thrown away. So this bead is DEFERRED BEHIND THE FLEET MIGRATION and no seat should pick it up before then. It is not closed, because the underlying fact has not changed and is not in dispute.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS THE REASON NOT TO CLOSE IT: packs/tiny's handoff and clock-out skills still tell a transient seat that deliver commits the staged set, and tinytown-nxoqe made that false on this same flight. These are documents a seat reads as instructions rather than as reference, so a seat following them before the migration is told something untrue about what its delivery will do. That cost is accepted by this deferral rather than eliminated by it -- which is the honest way to hold it, and is why this note says so plainly instead of recording a clean park.

NOTE THE CONTRAST WITH HIS D9, which is the same recommendation on a neighbouring bead and which he ruled A, fly it next flight. The distinction is worth keeping because it is reusable: fleet-28z33 is documentation ABOUT HOW WE WORK, which the migration will rewrite anyway; fleet-6eb1o is test hermeticity, which survives the migration unchanged and so is worth fixing now. He split two beads the operator had bundled, and split them on that line.

Still true, and the deferral ('until fleet migrates') has lifted. packs/tiny/skills/clock-out/SKILL.md:20 and packs/tiny/skills/handoff/SKILL.md:46 still say deliver commits the staged set; core/src/item/deliver.rs:55/185 has the DELIVERED AS-IS path.

title: the store opener's bd resolution is never executed by a test — BdStores::resolved() is reached only from Engine::on, whose two callers are both production entry points
description:
## Why

tinytown-tnkuq.83 landed the store opener's bd resolution and PROVED Bd::at_bin with a real arm (an_absolute_binary_runs_where_a_bare_name_cannot in fleet/core/tests/store.rs, red-proved twice from different materials). What it did NOT prove is the wiring: BdStores::resolved() is constructed at exactly one site, fleet/cli/src/flights.rs:166 inside Engine::on, and Engine::on is called only from fleet/cli/src/main.rs:558 and fleet/cli/src/item.rs:332 — both production entry points, neither a test. Confirmed by the reviewer with a positive control in the same grep. So the four lines that resolve the binary and hand it to the store are proved by cargo check alone, and an error in them would put the flight pass back on the bare name — the exact failure tinytown-tnkuq.83 exists to end, silently, because the fallback is the bare name by design (its D1, accepted).

## Why it was not done there

The arm has exactly one possible home: the cfg(test) module inside fleet/cli/src/flights.rs, because fleet-cli is a [[bin]] and no integration test can name Engine. That module is the region Alberto's ruling D-pre1 on flight tinytown-tjgr7 fenced, to keep builder-1's rebase on tinytown-6ravv.14 cheap — and tinytown-6ravv.14's own converted arms live in that same module. Two deliveries into one cfg(test) module are a park.

## What lands

1. One cfg(test) arm in fleet/cli/src/flights.rs that constructs BdStores::resolved() — or Engine::on — with the process PATH set to a service-shaped PATH holding no bd and a shim reachable only by absolute path, and asserts the store runs the shim. The shape to copy is fleet/core/tests/store.rs's an_absolute_binary_runs_where_a_bare_name_cannot, which already puts the control and the proof on one PATH.
2. Red proof by breaking the real wiring (BdStores::resolved made to return the bare name), watching the arm fail, restoring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 the new arm is green, with the selector's filtered count printed beside it so the green is not an empty selection.
- AC2 the arm FAILS when BdStores::resolved() is made to return PathBuf::from(store::BD), and the mutant COMPILES — a build failure is not a red.
- AC3 no other hunk in flights.rs; the diff in that file is the cfg(test) arm alone.
notes:
ALBERTO'S RULING on flight tinytown-tjgr7's decision log, 2026-09-17: D7 ADOPTED A, the operator's recommendation -- unpark once the fenced work lands, and test in place. Verbatim from the log: 'D7: A'. So this bead stays held behind builder-1's tinytown-6ravv.14 and is UNPARKED BY THE LANDING OF THAT BEAD, not by a calendar: the arm's home is the cfg(test) module inside flights.rs that his own pre-flight ruling D-pre1 fenced for the duration of that work. Option B (restructure production so the path is reachable from an integration test) NOT taken -- it spends production structure on a test for a path nobody has seen fail. Option C (accept it untested and say so in the code) NOT taken. WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the thing under test is the store opener's resolution of the issue-tracker binary, reached only from one place whose two callers are both production entry points, so the arm has to construct that reach rather than call a helper -- and re-read the file before trusting that sentence, because the fence lifting means that file has just changed.

BdStores::resolved() is now cli/src/runs.rs:53, built only inside Engine::on (runs.rs:80), whose sole caller is cli/src/main.rs:577 (observe_loop); the item.rs caller is gone. fleet/cli/src/flights.rs no longer exists. The Engine is now the controller's run seam, not the flight engine. The cfg(test) module to extend is cli/src/runs.rs:224, which already uses FakeStore; the shape to copy is core/tests/store.rs:119. The 'fenced behind tinytown-6ravv.14' hold and the D7 unpark condition are moot (flights.rs deleted), so this is unblocked. Corrections: (a) agent_pinned_version is NOT the adapter's read — it is policy.claude_code_pin, already paired with the live read in the controller (fleet/controller/src/run.rs:518 and :820-821) and published on the projection; only agent_live_version comes from adapter::version(). Both rows are cheaper than the spec thought. (b) load_at_takeoff reads platform::load_average_5m() (fleet/controller/src/platform/mod.rs:230), the five-minute sample, renamed and re-sampled by a7f9631f9; the row's value says which sample it is. (c) model_per_role cannot come from the flight's seat steps: the core formula pins no model (zero occurrences in fleet/packs/core/formulas/item.toml) and every real inputs.toml carries role with no model; the per-role model is resolved by Policy::model_for at seat render (fleet/controller/src/lifecycle.rs:454), which is where the reader belongs. The two account rows and the two variances stay pending. The neighbouring arm is a_reading_the_seam_answers_fills_its_row_and_leaves_pending (fleet/core/tests/fly.rs:894); the all-eight-absent assertion lives in fleet/cli/tests/plan.rs:319. The takeoff's one stdout line (fly.rs:229) still names no readings count, so that line of the spec is still owed.

---

## Why

Found at the rehearsal's step 17 (tinytown-tnkuq.20, 2026-09-14): flight tinytown-41z31's inputs.toml carries an empty [readings] table and a [pending] table with all eight readings ABSENT BY NAME — account, account_usage, agent_live_version, agent_pinned_version, load_at_takeoff, model_per_role, variance_network, variance_sampling — "no reader on this tree". tinytown-tnkuq.16 designed the seam (the Wiring's readings trait, one method answering the rows it can read) and shipped the cli's implementation answering none, as the partial half of its R2, for a later slice to fill row by row. No open bead carries that slice.

## What the in-repo harness had

The dispatch note names the box's load and the seat's runway at the moment of dispatch (brain/architect-role.md, the cap-concurrent-dispatches order); the porter pins the agent's version (make porter-status prints the pinned and live versions); the runway board reads the account's usage window. A flight report that cannot say the load at takeoff, the agent version it flew on or the account window it spent is one a later reader cannot price, which is the number the flights PRD's success metric needs.

## What

Readers for the rows the tree can answer, filled one row at a time on the seam tinytown-tnkuq.16 left: agent_pinned_version and agent_live_version from the adapter (the porter's status already resolves both), load_at_takeoff from the platform's load average, account and account_usage where the agent exposes them, model_per_role from the flight policy's roles. The two variances stay pending until something measures them. A row the tree cannot answer stays ABSENT BY NAME, never a guess.

## Implementation

Where: the readings seam tinytown-tnkuq.16 left — the `Wiring` readings trait in fleet/core (one method answering the rows it can read) and fleet/cli's implementation of it, which answers none. The row names are the eight keys `fleet fly` writes under `[pending]` in a flight's inputs.toml.

Change, one reader per row the tree can answer: `agent_pinned_version` and `agent_live_version` from the adapter's version read (fleet/controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs, the `version` method the roster poll already calls); `load_at_takeoff` from the platform's load average (fleet/controller/src/platform/macos.rs, the `getloadavg` extern the belt already reads); `model_per_role` from the flight's seat steps (the `model` per role that `fleet fly` pins in inputs.toml). `account`, `account_usage`, `variance_network` and `variance_sampling` stay under `[pending]` with the same sentence until a reader exists. Each answered row moves from `[pending]` to `[readings]`; the takeoff's stdout names how many rows were read and how many stay pending.

Test, in fleet/core's fly tests beside the existing `[pending]` arm: a fly through a rig whose readings seam answers the four rows writes them under `[readings]` with the values the seam gave and leaves exactly four keys under `[pending]`; a second arm with a seam answering a wrong load value against the platform's own read is caught by comparing the two. The red proof: the readers removed, all eight keys read ABSENT BY NAME as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A takeoff on this box writes agent_pinned_version, agent_live_version, load_at_takeoff and model_per_role under [readings] with the values the porter's status and the platform print, and leaves the rows it cannot read under [pending] unchanged.
- A red proof: a reader answering a wrong value for a known row is caught by an arm comparing it to the platform's own read.
- Gate: touched suites green; reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

title: fleet: a foreground flight retires a parked seat it can price nothing about — session.retired carries context_tokens null and transcript false because a foreground run has no collector
notes:
Found by the builder of tinytown-tnkuq.50, 2026-09-13, and confirmed at its review by builder-2.

MEASURED, not theorised. Writing tinytown-tnkuq.50's live arm on fleet fly's FOREGROUND loop, the arm went red on the retire's cost: session.retired carried context_tokens null and transcript false. The cause the builder gives: the session id a transcript is keyed by is recorded by the COLLECTOR, and a foreground flight has none. The arm was moved to plant_a_fresh_projection + tick_until_closed, where it reads WINDOW and TURNS, and went green — so the gap is the foreground path's and not the act's.

WHY IT MATTERS: a flight flown in the foreground retires seats with no cost attached, so the run's own accounting is blind for exactly the mode a person watches. Everything the tick does is priced; the same act through fly is not.

STEPS TO REPRODUCE: park an item with fleet ask on a foreground fleet fly flight so the parked act retires the asking seat; read session.retired off the stream. Expect context_tokens and transcript populated as the tick's retire populates them; observe null and false.

Not tinytown-tnkuq.50's to fix: that bead's Slice boundary is the gate object and its verbs, and the foreground loop's collector is neither. Filed rather than carried.

title: a_loop_killed_between_a_dispatch_and_its_event_restarts_without_dispatching_twice hangs: the stub builder loses a git add race, fleet deliver answers 'nothing is staged' on a loop, and the arm runs for 100+ minutes against a 494s baseline
description:
A FLAKE IN A LANDED ARM, measured in two independent runs by two seats on 2026-09-13.

THE ARM is tinytown-tnkuq.47's restart arm in fleet/cli/tests/flight.rs — the one that kills the foreground loop between a dispatch's order note and its event, restarts, and proves no second dispatch. It was demanded at that bead's first return and accepted at its third delivery, where it passed in 77.033s taken alone by the reviewer.

MEASUREMENT 1 (builder-2's subagent, reported to builder-1 by message, 2026-09-13): the arm hung for 102 MINUTES against a baseline of 494s. Diagnosed there rather than guessed: its fixture carries 7 events and NO session.crashed at all, and its stub builder lost a git add race, so fleet deliver answered 'nothing is staged' 120 times in a loop.

MEASUREMENT 2 (builder-1, the same day, independently and before reading that diagnosis): in a full workspace run at --test-threads 2 over tinytown-tnkuq.49's tree, the same arm was still running at 13m42s while the suite's progress counter sat at 149 of 842. The reviewer's own earlier run of that arm ALONE took 77.033s. So it is not simply slow under reduced parallelism; it has a hang mode.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN RUNTIME: this arm is the only proof that the advance holds nothing between calls — that a call dying between an act and its event leaves the act's note and the next fold reads it rather than dispatching twice. An arm that hangs is an arm people start skipping, and this is not one to skip. It is also now the single slowest thing in the fleet suite on a box where suite time is already the fleet's binding constraint.

NOT DIAGNOSED FURTHER BY EITHER SEAT: whether the git add race is in the stub builder's own shell or in the rig's sequencing, and whether the missing session.crashed in the fixture is deliberate (the arm kills a loop rather than crashing a seat) or the hole the race falls through.

title: The epic's boundary rule claims lessons-check guards all of fleet/, but that tool reads only fleet/docs/lessons/ — and a roster seat's chosen name sits in fleet/controller/tests/observe.rs today
description:
## Why

Found at builder-2's review of tinytown-tnkuq.66 (flight 10, manifest tinytown-1dq0f), incidentally — the bead under review neither introduced nor touched the offending file.

Every child of fleet-tnkuq carries this rule verbatim: 'nothing under fleet/ names this repository, a roster seat's chosen name, a seat directory or a bead id — python3 fleet/tools/lessons-check rc 0, part of the landing gate under fleet'. The rule names a scope (all of fleet/) and then names a tool as its enforcement.

The tool's scope is narrower than the rule's. fleet/tools/lessons-check's own docstring, line 2: 'the one reader of fleet/docs/lessons/'. Its roster() reads the chosen names and seat directories out of the rendered roster block as needles — 20 of them by its own output — and applies them to the lesson documents, not to the tree.

MEASURED, and this is the live instance: fleet/controller/tests/observe.rs carries "Rook" three times, a roster seat's chosen name (builder-1's), including as a chosen_name fixture value at line 46 and an assertion at line 804. Present at f06aa969b and unchanged at c6e296ad3 — 3 occurrences either side, and tinytown-tnkuq.66's diff touched that file in 0 files, so it is nobody's regression and has simply never been caught. lessons-check reads rc 0 on every one of those landings, correctly, because the file is outside what it reads.

Why it matters beyond tidiness: the whole point of the boundary is that fleet/ carries nothing of this repository before it leaves for its own home (D10, the snapshot). A guard whose scope is narrower than the rule it is cited for means every fleet bead's author, builder and reviewer has been quoting a green that never measured the claim. That is the same defect class as tinytown-tg0f5 and tinytown-artmd, in a third instrument.

## What lands

A decision first, then the work. Either the rule's scope narrows to what the tool checks, or the tool's scope widens to the rule — and the second needs care, because a needle like a two-letter seat directory or a common word would false-positive across a Rust tree, which is presumably why the tool was pointed at documents in the first place.

Then: the live instance in fleet/controller/tests/observe.rs is cleaned, whichever way the decision goes, because a seat's chosen name in a test fixture is the clearest possible case and no reading of the rule permits it.

## Decisions for whoever specs this

D1 — widen the tool to the tracked tree under fleet/, or narrow the rule's wording to the lesson documents. Recommended: widen, because the rule is the one the snapshot depends on; but the needle set needs a measured false-positive count over fleet/ before that is safe.
D2 — whether the cleaned fixture value is a neutral placeholder or drawn from a names list the tool also checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The false-positive count of the current 20 roster needles over the tracked tree under fleet/ is measured and quoted, before any widening lands.
- Whichever way D1 goes, grep -rnw for each roster chosen name over the tracked tree under fleet/ answers 0, with the count quoted and a positive control proving the search can see a name that IS present.
- python3 fleet/tools/lessons-check rc 0, with a red-prove: a needle planted in a file inside the new scope must make it exit non-zero, quoted, and the plant removed.
- The rule's wording in the epic and in any child that quotes it agrees with the tool's actual scope after this lands.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -rnw 'Rook' fleet/controller/tests/observe.rs` — 3 hits, including a `chosen_name` fixture value at line 46 and an assertion at line 804. "Rook" is a roster seat's chosen name.
2. `python3 fleet/tools/lessons-check` — rc 0, `boundary clean`.
3. Read `fleet/tools/lessons-check` line 2: "the one reader of `fleet/docs/lessons/`". The file in step 1 is outside what it reads, so the green is correct and the rule it is cited for is not enforced.
4. Confirm it is nobody's regression: the hits are present at `f06aa969b` and unchanged at `c6e296ad3`, with 0 files touched in that diff.

Second half, found at tinytown-tnkuq.66's re-delivery: `lessons-check` is NOT part of `make fleet-test`, so even within its own scan set a full green suite says nothing about this class.
notes:
SECOND SCOPE PROBLEM IN THE SAME GUARD (2026-09-13T11:12:50Z read from date -u, builder-2, found at tinytown-tnkuq.66's re-delivery and recorded here rather than as a third bead): lessons-check IS NOT PART OF make fleet-test. tinytown-tnkuq.66's builder put a bead id in a doc comment under fleet/controller/src, lessons-check exited 1 naming it — correctly, because a bead id carries this repository's name inside it — and the full suite would never have caught it. So the boundary rule every fleet bead quotes is enforced by a tool that (a) reads only fleet/docs/lessons/ and (b) is not in the suite that gates a landing. Both halves belong in this bead's decision: widening the scan set is worth little if nothing runs it at the gate.

The post-split cleanup bead named in the close reason is fleet-mdw.

title: the transient retire's pid-liveness reading answers yes for a defunct child
description:
## Why

`transient::retire` verifies from outside that nothing of the seat holds RAM,
and one of its readings is the pid the roster gave before the stop: it refuses
with "pid N, which the roster gave for `<seat>` before the stop, is still a live
process". That reading answers YES for a DEFUNCT child — a process that has
exited and whose parent has not reaped it — because a zombie still holds a pid
table entry and answers a liveness probe.

It is reachable through the adapter's own adoption rule. `claude_code::start`
watches a start for `[controller] start_watch_seconds` and, for a child still
running when the window closes, pushes it onto `adopted` and reaps it at the
NEXT `start` (`sweep_adopted`). So between such a child's exit and the next
spawn on that machine, its pid is a zombie — and a retire taken in that window
refuses, having ALREADY dropped the seat-list row and the session-table row. The
refusal says so and asks for the finish by hand; the flight's advance reads it
as "could not be retired" and the item's act fails on every later tick, because
the row it needs is gone.

Measured on this box while building tinytown-tnkuq.48, in the cli flight suite's
own fixture: `ps -o pid,ppid,args -p 59647` answered `59647 55253 <defunct>`
while `fleet seat retire` refused on that same pid. The fixture reached the
window by keeping its stub agent alive past the 30s watch; a real provider's
`--bg` returns at once, which is why nothing has met this in production. The
fixture was changed to exit inside the window rather than leaving the reading
uncorrected.

## What to decide

Whether the liveness reading should tell a zombie from a running process — on
this platform a `ps -o state` read, or `waitpid(WNOHANG)` where the caller is
the parent — and whether the retire should reap an adopted child of its own
process before taking the reading.

## Acceptance

The transient suite gains an arm that leaves a defunct child of the test process
behind, names its pid on the roster, and asserts the retire completes rather
than refusing; the control is the same arm against a pid that is genuinely
running, which must still refuse.
notes:
Moved from the tinytown board on 2026-09-22, where it was tinytown-oabpj; that bead is closed there with a pointer here. Edges to beads that stayed on the tinytown board, not carried across: discovered-from tinytown-tnkuq.48.
POST-SPLIT CORRECTION (2026-09-23 sweep, checked against HEAD 44c3736). Still true. controller/src/transient.rs:1766-1774 refuses on process_alive(pid)==Some(true); macOS is kill(pid,0) (platform/macos.rs:215-227) and Linux is /proc/<pid> existing (platform/linux.rs:54-59). Both answer yes for a zombie.

title: fleet review --return under a spawned reviewer reassigns the item to the reviewer, not the builder
description:
## Why

Under review `spawned` the flight gives a delivered item to the reviewer seat
under an order of kind `review`, so the order index's `seat` names the REVIEWER
while the review is open (flights PRD R14; the spec of tinytown-tnkuq.48 asks
for exactly that, "so a reader sees who holds it and the reviewer's fleet review
runs against an item it holds").

`fleet review --return` reads the builder to hand the item back to off that same
index — `fleet/core/src/item/review.rs`, the return's own comment: "The builder
is the order index's seat: the record of who was given this item, which is the
one place that says where a return goes." Under `spawned` that reads the
reviewer, so a return reassigns the item to the seat that wrote the verdict and
rings it. Measured on the scratch project through the shipped binary while
building tinytown-tnkuq.48: the run printed `RETURNED, NOT RUNG: no live session
for transient-1` where transient-1 was the reviewer's own name.

It is not a defect that breaks the flight: the advance's return act reassigns
the item to the fresh builder in the same act, and the ring lands on an absent
seat. It is a wrong line on the record for as long as it stands, and a person
reading the item between the verdict and the next tick sees the reviewer holding
its own return.

## What to decide

Whether a return under a spawned reviewer should reassign to the LAST BUILDER —
readable from the item's last delivery note's first line, or from the order
index the review order replaced — or whether the flight's own reassignment a
moment later is enough and the return should leave the assignee alone when the
index says kind `review`.

## Acceptance

The review suite gains an arm over an item whose order index carries kind
`review`: `fleet review --return` leaves the record naming whoever the decision
says, and the arm asserts the name rather than that a reassignment happened.

If the review panel returns (fleet-6ywp53), carry the rule that a return names the last builder, not the order-index seat.

title: State::Crashed has no producer: session.crashed is only written on a start failure, and that path holds the item rather than announcing it — so R34's park-at-the-crash is correct code with no live path into it
description:
Measured at tinytown-tnkuq.47's review, on the tree that landed as d5d95812b.

session.crashed has exactly ONE writer under fleet/: fleet/controller/src/effect.rs:264, the StartOutcome::Failed branch of spawn_woken. That branch returns Err(cause) and writes no session.spawned — the Ok branch at effect.rs:256 is the only writer of SESSION_SPAWNED. A control on the same search (SESSION_SPAWNED, whose writer is nameable) proves the search can find writers; transient.rs:859 only READS the kind.

On the failing path the spawner refusal makes the dispatch act write item.held rather than announcing, so the item never reaches a state a crash could act on.

CONSEQUENCE: flight::fold's State::Crashed, the advance's crash arm, and R34's park-at-the-crash are all correct code with no live path into them. Every arm exercising them drives a synthetic stream. Nothing is wrong with the code; what is missing is a producer for a mid-turn seat death.

WHERE IT BELONGS: tinytown-tnkuq.73 is the crash re-dispatch (behind tinytown-tnkuq.48) and is the bead that will care. The question this one asks is narrower and comes first: does anything intend to write session.crashed for a seat that already spawned, and if so which layer? The controller's revive/halt work (tinytown-tnkuq.6) is the neighbouring surface.

NOT A DEFECT IN tinytown-tnkuq.47, which was specced to build the park and did. Raised so the next reader of R34 does not believe the path is live.

title: bd init inside a linked worktree puts .beads/ in the repository's MAIN worktree, so fleet land's export gate refuses on a project that lives in a linked worktree
description:
Measured on bd 1.2.2 by the builder of tinytown-tnkuq.47, in a scratch repo: running bd init from inside a LINKED git worktree creates .beads/ in the repository's main worktree rather than beside the cwd. fleet's Bd::export writes to <project root>/.beads/issues.jsonl, so for a project whose root IS a linked worktree that path names a directory nothing created, and land's export gate refuses with the store's export left nothing at that path.

Where it bites: tinytown-tnkuq.47's AC2 rig flies a real flight against a project in a linked worktree (it has to be one, because land refuses a primary checkout). The rig works around it by creating the directory itself. Nothing in fleet does, so a real project set up the same way meets the refusal.

Not diagnosed: whether this is bd's intended behaviour for worktrees, whether a --db or -C flag steers it, or whether fleet should create the directory rather than assume it. Any of the three is a fine answer; the measurement is that the default path does not work.

title: Prove the per-row config directory WITHHOLDS the person's configuration, not only that the config root relocates — Q1e's core claim is unmeasured
description:
## Why

Filed at builder-2's review of tinytown-tnkuq.52 (flight 10, manifest tinytown-1dq0f), from that delivery's own not-proven section. The builder declared it; nobody found it by inspection.

tinytown-tnkuq.52 lands the isolated spawned seat and Q1e's whole point is that nothing from the person's home directory — settings, memory, instructions, servers — reaches a flight. What that delivery MEASURED, live and one variable apart, is that the configuration ROOT relocates: 'claude auth status' with nothing set answers projectsDirectory /Users/<person>/.claude/projects, and under a scratch directory with the credential knob defined-empty answers the scratch path. Both rc 0.

What is NOT measured is that nothing from the home directory is read ANYWAY. A second read of the home default alongside the scoped root would produce both of those readings and still leak.

AC1's clause 'a read of the person's home settings file from inside the session fails' was met — but the quoted refusal is 'Permission to use Read has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode'. That is the POSTURE refusing and it would answer identically under the person's own directory, so it evidences dontAsk and not isolation. It is the one clause of AC1 that is could-not-tell rather than passed, and it is the clause Q1e is actually about.

Why the builder could not close it: the arm needs a marker in the person's own home configuration, and writing there is not a subagent's act; reading it directly was refused by the auto-mode classifier. The reviewer did not close it either, for the first of those reasons — this touches Alberto's own configuration, so the act is his or taken with his word.

## What lands

A measurement, not a code change, recorded on this bead and folded into fleet/docs/lessons/claude-code.md A11 beside the roster consequence.

The arm, designed so it is cheap:
1. Read the person's ~/.claude/settings.json for a value the agent LOADS and renders in its own effective configuration — a distinctive setting, not the file's mere readability. File readability proves nothing: any process with filesystem permission can read any file, and the question is whether the AGENT loads it.
2. Start one session under a per-row config directory with the credential knob defined-empty and a posture that ALLOWS the read, so a refusal is the directory's answer and not the posture's.
3. Ask that session for its effective configuration and compare against (1), with a positive control in the same turn proving the read path works at all.
4. Isolation HOLDS when the person's distinctive value is absent from the isolated session's effective configuration; it LEAKS when present. A refusal is could-not-tell, not a hold — the third answer this arm must be able to express.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The arm above run on this box, both sides quoted from the commands' own output, with the positive control quoted.
- A11 carries the answer in one sentence, its Date extended, and its inventory test extended if a new row is warranted.
- Where the answer is LEAKS, a bug bead is filed against the isolation seam naming what reached the session, and this bead names it.
- No write into the person's home configuration without Alberto's word recorded on this bead first.
